magisterium.assessment_en: Criticism of the institutional status quo and the claim that the political system can be changed are not contrary to Catholic teaching; the Church does not prescribe a single mandatory constitutional or electoral model. The passage nevertheless makes political judgments about concrete actors and institutions, whose factual basis the provided texts do not make possible to independently verify.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching permits a plurality of political solutions for temporal matters, but this freedom does not mean that all moral goals are equally acceptable: politics must serve genuine human and social good. Scripture and Church teaching recall that authority is not meant for the benefit of officeholders, but of those cared for, and that political action is judged according to justice and responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: Institutional conservatism: nothing must change
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest discusses the crisis of the Constitutional Court and the model of electing judges that is more than 25 years old
sections.content_en:
Marić recalls that Žižić wrote in a column that it is difficult to classify Plenković in terms of worldview, but that he shows some conservative traits through institutional continuity. The guest clarifies that the Prime Minister does not define himself as a conservative. In him, however, he sees a desire to **maintain the status quo**, which he calls **institutional conservatism**. Things should stay as they are.

As an example, he cites the current crisis of the **Constitutional Court**. The Prime Minister, Žižić says, insists on a model of electing constitutional judges that has existed for more than 25 years. The logic, according to the guest, is that what exists is proven and tested, while changes could bring something worse and something that can no longer be controlled. In an ideological sense, however, Plenković is certainly not a conservative.

Marić asks whether conserving for the sake of conserving can be called an ideology at all. Žižić replies that the question is what one wants to preserve: values and principles or institutions. In his opinion, political institutions can be changed, but Croatia is in that sense "quite pronounced." He recalls that **every attempt to reform the electoral and political system has been thwarted**, primarily by HDZ, joined by other mainstream parties. Bottom-up initiatives are suppressed, for example through the prevention of **referendum initiatives** or the actions of the Constitutional Court.

Žižić does not believe that institutional changes alone can change society. Still, he sees no reason why the electoral or political system should not be changed. He contrasts such conservatism with American conservatism, such as that advocated by the **Republican Party**. That one is distinctly pro-market and attributes moral power to the market, which Žižić doubts. He assesses that such conservatism would be difficult to impose in Croatia.

sections.subtitle: Štrajk u Zagrebačkom holdingu: građani su reagirali kao potrošači
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava kako je gradska vlast manipulirala podacima o plaćama radnika
sections.content:
Žižić zatim prelazi na štrajk u **Zagrebačkom holdingu** i **Čistoći**. Po njemu, štrajk je pokazao koliko je duboko **tržišna logika** prodrla u sve sektore i slojeve hrvatskog društva. Ta je logika, kaže, prvenstveno pomogla zagrebačkoj gradskoj vlasti, koja je štrajk htjela suzbiti.

Gradska vlast je, prema gostu, vješto **manipulirala podacima o plaćama** kako bi u javnosti stvorila animozitet prema radnicima i prikazala ih kao preplaćene i povlaštene. Namjerno su, navodi, objavljivane plaće iz mjeseca u kojem je isplaćen regres, kako bi iznosi izgledali veći.

Najvažniji zaključak Žižić vidi u reakciji javnosti. Ljudi su reagirali **kao potrošači, a ne kao građani, solidarni kršćani i katolici ili članovi zajednice**. Gledali su samo troškove, koristi i cijene. Ta je logika, ističe, išla u korist **Možemo**. Stranku u Hrvatskoj svi nazivaju ljevičarskom, ali ona to po Žižiću nije: riječ je o **liberalnoj stranci**. Marić dodaje da se to tada najbolje vidjelo.

Gost tvrdi da je štrajk pokazao koliko je Možemo udaljen od klasičnog radništva, koje nije njegovo biračko tijelo. Biračko tijelo te stranke opisuje kao ljude koji s laptopom odlaze raditi u IT tvrtke, udruge i kulturni sektor. Za njih je štrajk značio trošak taksija, dodatno hodanje i neugodu. Pritom se, kaže, ne pitaju što će biti s poslovima poput vozača tramvaja. Ti poslovi nisu atraktivni i ljudi se za njih ne otimaju ako im se ne ponude barem natprosječne plaće. „A ako nećete imati to, imat ćete strance“, upozorava Žižić.

Marić dodaje da je prijedlog „dovest ćemo strance“ bio najbolji filter protivnika štrajka. Navodni ljevičari koji bi se trebali zalagati za radnička prava odjednom su postali „veliki tržištarci“.

Žižić je osobno štrajk doživio i kao trenutak u kojem se **ponovno rodila solidarnost**. Dok je vozio suprugu, prijevoz su ponudili i susjedima koje inače samo pozdravljaju u liftu. Ipak zaključuje: „melje nas, taj liberalizam nas drobi“. Liberalizam je, kaže, iznimno prisutan u medijima i drugačiji glasovi teško dopiru do javnosti. Iskreno priznaje da je i u vlastitom katoličkom miljeu primijetio dosta protivljenja štrajku.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na solidarnosti s radnicima i kritika svođenja javnih službi na trošak ili neugodnost dobro se uklapaju u katolički nauk o dostojanstvu rada i odgovornosti za bližnjega. Ipak, odlomak iznosi političke ocjene i široke generalizacije koje nisu same po sebi crkveni nauk, a štrajk se mora vrednovati uz njegove uvjete, granice i zaštitu općega dobra.
concerns: U prikazu se reakcije građana uopćeno tumače kao potrošačka sebičnost, iako nezadovoljstvo prekidom usluge samo po sebi ne dokazuje odsutnost solidarnosti; katolički pristup traži istinu, razboritost i poniznost u prosudbi složenih društvenih okolnosti.

Tvrdnju da će zbog nedostatka domaćih radnika biti potrebno zaposliti strance ne bi trebalo shvatiti kao svođenje ljudi na zamjenjivu radnu snagu: katoličko socijalno učenje naglašava solidarnost s radnicima bez granica i dostojanstvo imigranata.

Štrajk je u katoličkom nauku legitimno, ali krajnje sredstvo pod opravdanim uvjetima i unutar pravednih granica; kod ključnih službi mora se osigurati ono što je potrebno zajednici. Odlomak ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se procijenilo jesu li ti uvjeti u konkretnom štrajku bili ispunjeni.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička solidarnost nije samo osjećaj naklonosti prema određenoj skupini, nego spremnost da se štite prava radnika i traže pravedni odnosi, uz obzir prema cijeloj zajednici. Zato kritika tržišnog svođenja rada na trošak može biti opravdana, ali kršćanska prosudba treba istodobno uzeti u obzir radnike, korisnike javnih usluga i opće dobro te poticati dijalog i rješenja, a ne samo sukob.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on solidarity with workers and the criticism of reducing public services to a cost or inconvenience fit well within Catholic teaching on the dignity of work and responsibility for one's neighbor. Nevertheless, the passage makes political judgments and broad generalizations that are not in themselves Church teaching, and a strike must be evaluated alongside its conditions, limits, and the protection of the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic solidarity is not merely a feeling of affection for a particular group, but a readiness to protect workers' rights and pursue just relations, with regard for the entire community. Therefore, criticism of the market reduction of work to an expense can be justified, but Christian evaluation must simultaneously take into account workers, users of public services, and the common good, encouraging dialogue and solutions, not merely conflict.
concerns_en: In the presentation, citizens' reactions are interpreted generally as consumer selfishness, even though dissatisfaction with service disruption does not in itself prove the absence of solidarity; a Catholic approach calls for truth, prudence, and humility in judging complex social circumstances.

The assertion that the lack of domestic workers will make it necessary to hire foreigners should not be understood as reducing people to replaceable labor: Catholic social teaching emphasizes solidarity with workers across borders and the dignity of immigrants.

In Catholic teaching, a strike is a legitimate but last-resort measure under justified conditions and within just limits; essential services must secure what is necessary for the community. The passage does not provide sufficient data to judge whether these conditions were met in the specific strike.

sections.subtitle_en: Strike at Zagrebački holding: citizens reacted as consumers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest explains how city authorities manipulated worker wage data
sections.content_en:
Žižić then turns to the strike at **Zagrebački holding** and **Čistoća**. According to him, the strike showed how deeply **market logic** has penetrated all sectors and strata of Croatian society. That logic, he says, primarily helped the Zagreb city government, which wanted to suppress the strike.

The city government, according to the guest, skillfully **manipulated wage data** to create animosity toward workers in the public and present them as overpaid and privileged. Wages from the month in which the holiday allowance was paid were deliberately published, he states, so that the amounts would look larger.

Žižić sees the most important conclusion in the public reaction. People reacted **as consumers, not as citizens, solidary Christians and Catholics, or members of the community**. They looked only at costs, benefits, and prices. That logic, he emphasizes, worked to the advantage of **Možemo**. Everyone in Croatia calls the party leftist, but according to Žižić it is not: it is **a liberal party**. Marić adds that this was seen best back then.

The guest claims that the strike showed how far Možemo is from the classic working class, which is not its electorate. He describes that party's electorate as people who go with laptops to work in IT companies, associations, and the cultural sector. For them, the strike meant taxi fares, additional walking, and discomfort. At the same time, he says, they do not ask themselves what will happen to jobs like tram drivers. Those jobs are not attractive and people do not scramble for them unless offered at least above-average wages. "And if you won't have that, you will have foreigners," Žižić warns.

Marić adds that the proposal "we will bring in foreigners" was the best filter for opponents of the strike. Alleged leftists who should advocate for workers' rights suddenly became "great free-marketeers."

Žižić personally experienced the strike also as a moment in which **solidarity was reborn**. While driving his wife, they also offered a ride to neighbors they otherwise only greet in the elevator. Still, he concludes: "it is grinding us down, that liberalism is crushing us." Liberalism, he says, is extremely present in the media and different voices have a hard time reaching the public. He honestly admits that in his own Catholic milieu he noticed a lot of opposition to the strike as well.

sections.subtitle: Srbija nije Hrvatska, ali su „tri poljupca“ i „ruzmarin“ stigli do hrvatskih studenata
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava kako su njegovi studenti saznali za kampanju u Srbiji
sections.content:
Marić se vraća temi konzervativizma i statusa quo te otvara pitanje usporedbe sa susjednom Srbijom. Hrvatski mediji, kaže, znaju objavljivati velike naslove poput „otišao je Orban, pao je Vučić“ i pitati je li Plenković idući. Vidio je to na Indexu. Srpske studente pritom veličaju na štetu hrvatskih, koje prikazuju kao pasivne. Marić pita može li se situacija uopće uspoređivati.

Žižić odgovara da se usporedba **nikako ne može povući**, ali da su neke stvari vrlo zanimljive. Otvoreno priznaje da su njegovi studenti **prilično politički neinformirani**. Nedostaje im i politička informiranost i politička pismenost, odnosno poznavanje institucija. Ipak je na predavanju primijetio da ih situacija u Srbiji odjednom zanima. Pitao ih je koliko ih je čulo za „tri poljupca“ i za „ruzmarin“. U oba slučaja potvrdno je odgovorilo oko **75 posto**.

To pripisuje društvenim mrežama, **TikToku** i video sadržajima. Kampanja u Srbiji morala je zaobilaziti televizije pa se orijentirala na digitalni prostor. Riječ je o studentima prosječne dobi između 21 i 23 godine. Žižić procjenjuje da će pobjeda studentske liste izazvati neku vrstu **lančane reakcije** koja će se postupno osjetiti i u Hrvatskoj. Teško mu je predvidjeti kako, ali sigurno ne onako kako to najavljuju pojedini mediji.

Marić staje u obranu hrvatske političke kulture. Smatra da je Hrvatska politički kulturnija od susjeda i da konzervativizam ponekad može biti pozitivan jer sprječava da itko zavlada u potpunosti. Uspoređuje srpske medije poput Informera i Kurira s emisijom na HRT-u u kojoj se otvoreno raspravljalo o Plenkoviću. Žižić se slaže da u Hrvatskoj postoji više konvencionalnosti, pristojnosti i suzdržanosti. Kad Marić doda da tu ima i „naše plašljivosti“, gost potvrđuje da ima i srama i straha da se neke stvari kažu.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom iznosi opisne političke procjene o informiranosti studenata, društvenim mrežama i razlikama između Hrvatske i Srbije; u njemu nema jasne tvrdnje koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Ipak, procjene o političkoj kulturi i mogućoj „lančanoj reakciji” ostaju spekulativne te ih je razborito iznositi bez neosnovanih generalizacija ili nacionalnog samouzvisivanja.
concerns: Usporedba Hrvatske i Srbije te tvrdnja da je Hrvatska politički kulturnija iznesene su kao procjene sudionika, a ne kao utvrđene činjenice ili katolička prosudba; bez dodatnih dokaza ne treba iz njih izvoditi opću moralnu ocjenu naroda.

Predviđanje da će pobjeda studentske liste u Srbiji izazvati lančanu reakciju u Hrvatskoj izričito je neizvjesno; teološki je problematično samo ako bi se politička pretpostavka prikazivala kao sigurna činjenica ili kao mjerilo kršćanske vjernosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička društvena prosudba traži istinoljubivost, uvažavanje složenosti i poniznost kad se analiziraju odnosi u društvu, umjesto da se politički događaji tumače samo kroz ideološke etikete. Politička informiranost može pomoći odgovornom sudjelovanju u zajedničkom životu, ali iz ovog odlomka nije moguće zaključiti što konkretno studenti znaju niti kakve bi posljedice srpski politički događaji imali u Hrvatskoj.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage mainly makes descriptive political assessments regarding student awareness, social networks, and differences between Croatia and Serbia; there is no clear assertion in it that would contradict Catholic teaching or Scripture. Nevertheless, assessments of political culture and a possible "chain reaction" remain speculative and are prudently presented without unfounded generalizations or national self-exaltation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic social judgment requires truthfulness, respect for complexity, and humility when analyzing relationships in society, rather than interpreting political events solely through ideological labels. Political awareness can help responsible participation in community life, but from this passage it is not possible to conclude what students concretely know or what consequences Serbian political events would have in Croatia.
concerns_en: The comparison between Croatia and Serbia and the claim that Croatia is politically more cultured are presented as participant assessments, not as established facts or Catholic judgment; without additional evidence, a general moral assessment of nations should not be derived from them.

The prediction that the victory of a student list in Serbia will trigger a chain reaction in Croatia is explicitly uncertain; it is theologically problematic only if a political assumption were presented as a certain fact or as a criterion of Christian fidelity.

sections.subtitle_en: Serbia is not Croatia, but "three kisses" and "rosemary" reached Croatian students
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest recounts how his students learned about the campaign in Serbia
sections.content_en:
Marić returns to the topic of conservatism and status quo and opens the question of comparison with neighboring Serbia. Croatian media, he says, know how to publish big headlines like "Orban is gone, Vučić has fallen" and ask whether Plenković is next. He saw that on Index. At the same time, Serbian students are glorified at the expense of Croatian ones, who are portrayed as passive. Marić asks whether the situation can be compared at all.

Žižić replies that a comparison **can by no means be drawn**, but that some things are very interesting. He openly admits that his students are **quite politically uninformed**. They lack both political information and political literacy, that is, knowledge of institutions. Yet at a lecture, he noticed that the situation in Serbia suddenly interested them. He asked them how many of them had heard of "three kisses" and of "rosemary." In both cases, about **75 percent** answered affirmatively.

He attributes this to social networks, **TikTok**, and video content. The campaign in Serbia had to bypass television stations, so it oriented itself to digital space. These are students with an average age between 21 and 23. Žižić assesses that the victory of the student list will cause a kind of **chain reaction** that will gradually be felt in Croatia as well. It is difficult for him to predict how, but certainly not in the way announced by certain media.

Marić stands up in defense of Croatian political culture. He believes that Croatia is politically more cultured than its neighbors and that conservatism can sometimes be positive because it prevents anyone from ruling completely. He compares Serbian media like Informer and Kurir with a show on HRT in which Plenković was openly debated. Žižić agrees that in Croatia there is more conventionality, decency, and restraint. When Marić adds that there is also "our timidity," the guest confirms that there is both shame and fear to say certain things.

sections.subtitle: SDP između socijaldemokracije i liberalizma: stranka bez radnika i s urbanim biračima koje osvaja Možemo
sections.screenshot_description: Gost analizira transformaciju SDP-a i gubitak urbanih birača
sections.content:
Marić pita što je danas SDP, osobito u kontekstu suradnje s Možemo. Je li to socijaldemokratska lijeva stranka ili je ušla u „liberalni mod“?

Žižić podsjeća da je SDP jedna od rijetkih hrvatskih stranaka koja ideološku oznaku nosi u samom nazivu. Transformacija **Saveza komunista** u socijaldemokratsku stranku bila je, kaže, nužna: prihvaćanjem demokracije nisu imali drugog izbora nego krenuti prema reformskom, demokratskom socijalizmu i socijaldemokraciji. Danas je to, uz nominalnu socijaldemokraciju, otišlo u **liberalizam**.

Glavni pokretač tog pomaka gost vidi u **promjeni društvene strukture**. Klasičnog radništva gotovo više nema, a ono za SDP u suvremenoj Hrvatskoj nikad nije posebno ni glasalo, osim možda na izborima 2000. SDP je uvijek bio stranka **uslužne klase**: inženjera, liječnika, nastavnika, obrazovanijih slojeva s boljim primanjima.

U taj se prostor, međutim, ubacio **Možemo**. Osvojio je urbanu populaciju, osobito u Zagrebu, gdje mnogim biračima djeluje prepoznatljivije i jasnije od SDP-a. SDP ipak ne može potpuno izgubiti jer je, za razliku od Možemo, i dalje oblik **nacionalne stranke**, teritorijalno prisutne u cijeloj Hrvatskoj, uz iznimke gdje je vrlo slab. Marić dodaje da biračka populacija SDP-a odumire, a Žižić potvrđuje da stranka ima stariju bazu, dok je Možemo u prednosti.

Među ljudima koji ne rade kognitivne poslove, nego u nižim uslužnim djelatnostima, trgovini ili proizvodnji, za SDP glasa vrlo malo njih. Zato njegove mjere ne nailaze na plodno tlo. Žižić podsjeća da se **politika rađa u društvu**, a ne samo u medijima, koliko god danas svi isticali važnost medijske pozornosti. SDP je, kaže, u jednom trenutku umjesto preostalog radništva odabrao skupine koje je smatrao zakinutijima, prije svega **rodne i seksualne manjine**. Marić primjećuje da je njih realno mnogo manje od radnika, pa se stranka time automatski suzila.

Žižić to najbolje vidi na primjeru Njemačke. Tamo klasično radništvo danas glasa za **AfD**, a ne za **SPD**, nekad najveću socijaldemokratsku i radničku stranku u Europi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi pretežno sociološku i stranačko-političku analizu te ne proturječi izravno katoličkom nauku. Ipak, prikaz radnika i rodnih ili seksualnih manjina uglavnom kao biračkih skupina može zamagliti da katolički nauk zahtijeva i dostojanstvo rada i poštovanje dostojanstva svake osobe, bez nepravedne diskriminacije.
concerns: Zaključak da političko usmjeravanje prema rodnim i seksualnim manjinama sužava stranku zato što su te skupine brojčano manje može zvučati kao svođenje osoba na njihovu političku korisnost; iz odlomka, međutim, nije jasno iznosi li se to kao izborna analiza ili kao moralni sud.

Odlomak ne razrađuje crkveno razlikovanje između poštovanja osoba i moralne prosudbe pojedinih postupaka; zato samo spominjanje tih skupina ne treba tumačiti ni kao odobravanje ni kao osudu crkvenog nauka.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički socijalni nauk rad vidi kao sudjelovanje u Božjem stvaralačkom djelu te naglašava prava radnika na pravednu plaću, dostojanstvene uvjete i udruživanje, pa je opravdano pitati zastupa li neka stranka stvarne potrebe radnika, a ne samo njihovu izbornu važnost. Istodobno, svaka osoba, bez obzira na seksualnu orijentaciju, mora biti poštovana i zaštićena od nepravedne diskriminacije; politička pripadnost ili veličina biračke skupine ne umanjuju njezino ljudsko dostojanstvo.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents a predominantly sociological and party-political analysis and does not directly contradict Catholic teaching. However, portraying workers and gender or sexual minorities mainly as voting groups can obscure the fact that Catholic teaching requires both the dignity of work and respect for the dignity of each person, without unjust discrimination.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic social teaching views work as participation in God's creative activity and emphasizes workers' rights to a just wage, decent conditions, and association, so it is legitimate to ask whether a party represents the real needs of workers and not merely their electoral importance. At the same time, every person, regardless of sexual orientation, must be respected and protected from unjust discrimination; political affiliation or the size of a voting group does not diminish their human dignity.
concerns_en: The conclusion that political orientation toward gender and sexual minorities narrows a party because those groups are numerically smaller can sound like reducing persons to their political utility; from the passage, however, it is not clear whether this is stated as electoral analysis or as a moral judgment.

The passage does not elaborate on the Church's distinction between respect for persons and moral judgment of particular actions; therefore, the mere mention of these groups should not be interpreted as either approval or condemnation of Church teaching.

sections.subtitle_en: SDP between social democracy and liberalism: a party without workers and with urban voters won over by Možemo
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest analyzes the transformation of SDP and the loss of urban voters
sections.content_en:
Marić asks what SDP is today, especially in the context of cooperation with Možemo. Is it a social democratic left party or has it entered "liberal mode"?

Žižić recalls that SDP is one of the few Croatian parties that bears an ideological designation in its very name. The transformation of the **League of Communists** into a social democratic party was, he says, necessary: by accepting democracy, they had no other choice than to head toward reformist, democratic socialism and social democracy. Today, alongside nominal social democracy, it has gone into **liberalism**.

The guest sees the main driver of that shift in the **change of social structure**. Classic working class is almost no more, and in contemporary Croatia it never particularly voted for SDP anyway, except perhaps in the 2000 elections. SDP was always a party of the **service class**: engineers, doctors, teachers, more educated strata with better incomes.

Into that space, however, **Možemo** inserted itself. It conquered the urban population, especially in Zagreb, where to many voters it seems more recognizable and clearer than SDP. Still, SDP cannot lose completely because, unlike Možemo, it is still a form of **national party**, territorially present throughout Croatia, with exceptions where it is very weak. Marić adds that SDP's voter population is dying out, and Žižić confirms that the party has an older base, while Možemo has the advantage.

Among people who do not do cognitive jobs, but work in lower service activities, trade, or manufacturing, very few vote for SDP. That is why its measures do not fall on fertile ground. Žižić recalls that **politics is born in society**, not just in the media, no matter how much everyone emphasizes the importance of media attention today. SDP, he says, at one point chose groups it considered more disadvantaged instead of the remaining working class, primarily **gender and sexual minorities**. Marić observes that there are realistically far fewer of them than workers, so the party thereby automatically narrowed itself.

Žižić sees this best in the example of Germany. There, the classic working class today votes for **AfD**, not for **SPD**, once the largest social democratic and workers' party in Europe.

sections.subtitle: Socijaldemokrati nestaju diljem Europe, a Možemo raste na ruševinama SDP-a
sections.screenshot_description: Gost nabraja europske zemlje u kojima su socijaldemokrati nestali iz parlamenta
sections.content:
Marić primjećuje da su europske stranke slične Možemo, poput **Podemosa** i drugih, u padu. Hrvatski Možemo, osobito nakon štrajka, kao da raste. Pita što Hrvatsku razlikuje.

Žižić stvar okreće: Možemo jest u rastu, ali istodobno **pada najveća lijeva stranka, SDP**. Marić to sažima kao „spojene posude“, što gost potvrđuje. Pad jedne velike socijaldemokratske stranke uklapa se, kaže, u **širi europski obrazac**. Socijaldemokrata više nema u **Mađarskoj** ni **Češkoj**, gdje nisu ni u parlamentu. U **Sloveniji** su jako oslabili, a nema ih više ni u **Bugarskoj**. Riječ je o državama u kojima su nekad bili vladajuće stranke. Socijaldemokrati negdje ostaju relevantni, ali općenito slabe.

Marić pita kako je u Srbiji prošao pokret koji spominje kao „Moramo“. Žižić odgovara da su ondje zeleno-lijeve opcije podržale studentsku listu, što ocjenjuje kao **stratešku prilagodbu**. Dodaje da je u Srbiji od stranaka u parlament ušla samo **Srpska napredna stranka**, koja je izgubila izbore. Srbija, ponavlja, nije usporediva s Hrvatskom, gdje treba pratiti druge procese.

Dinamiku između SDP-a i Možemo, najavljuje Žižić, najbolje će se objasniti kada razgovor dođe do njihove najavljene koalicije. Marić se s time slaže i zatvara ovaj tematski blok.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom opisuje izborna kretanja i prilagodbu političkih stranaka, bez tvrdnji o vjeri, moralu ili Svetom pismu koje bi bile u sukobu s katoličkim naukom. Njegovu političku analizu zato ne treba poistovjetiti s katoličkim vrednovanjem stranaka ili njihovih programa.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička prosudba političkih opcija ne počiva samo na njihovu rastu, padu ili sposobnosti da osvoje birače, nego i na tome služe li ljudskom dostojanstvu i općem dobru. U tom je okviru važno promatrati kako stranke odgovaraju na potrebe radnika: crkveni nauk ističe dostojanstvo rada te prava na pravednu plaću, sigurnost i udruživanje.

sections.subtitle_en: Social democrats are disappearing across Europe, while Možemo grows on the ruins of SDP
sections.screenshot_description_en: Guest lists European countries where social democrats disappeared from parliament
sections.content_en:
Marić observes that European parties similar to Možemo, such as **Podemos** and others, are in decline. Croatian Možemo, especially after the strike, seems to be growing. He asks what makes Croatia different.

Žižić turns things around: Možemo is indeed growing, but at the same time **the largest left party, SDP, is falling**. Marić summarizes this as "communicating vessels," which the guest confirms. The fall of a major social democratic party fits, he says, into a **broader European pattern**. Social democrats are no longer present in **Hungary** or the **Czech Republic**, where they are not even in parliament. In **Slovenia** they have weakened greatly, and they are no longer in **Bulgaria** either. These are states in which they were once governing parties. Social democrats remain relevant somewhere, but generally they are weakening.

Marić asks how the movement he mentions as "Moramo" fared in Serbia. Žižić replies that there green-left options supported the student list, which he assesses as a **strategic adjustment**. He adds that in Serbia, among parties, only the **Serbian Progressive Party** entered parliament, which lost the elections. Serbia, he repeats, is not comparable to Croatia, where other processes should be monitored.

The dynamics between SDP and Možemo, Žižić announces, will be best explained when the conversation turns to their announced coalition. Marić agrees with this and closes this thematic block.

sections.subtitle: Most: suverenisti koji bježe od ideoloških etiketa, a biračko tijelo im ne posustaje
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava zašto Most ima stabilno i vjerno biračko tijelo unatoč stalnim predviđanjima propasti
sections.content:
Nakon analize lijevog dijela spektra, voditelj **Marin Marić** prelazi na ostatak oporbe. Podsjeća da je Most prešao 10 posto potpore i da je sve prisutniji u medijima. Ipak, stranci se pripisuju vrlo različiti ideološki predznaci: negdje ih se naziva konzervativcima, negdje demokršćanima, a negdje im se lijepi etiketa populizma. U posljednje vrijeme najviše su se podigli na antikorupcijskoj tematici, pa Marić pita što je njihova suštinska ideologija.

Politolog **Jakov Žižić** odgovara da je Most svjesno bježao od ideoloških oznaka. Razlog vidi u njihovoj racionalnosti: razumiju da takve oznake u javnosti imaju negativno značenje. Žižić ističe da Most dobro prati raspoloženje građana i ima, kako kaže, dobre senzore za prepoznavanje javnog mnijenja. U ideološkom smislu, posebno kad je riječ o društvenim vrijednostima, stranka je po njegovoj ocjeni **konzervativna**. Program sadrži dosta odrednica demokršćanstva, ali se Most nikad ne bi nazvao demokršćanskom strankom. O sebi govori kao o **suverenističkoj stranci**.

Žižić naglašava jednu zanimljivost: Mostu biračka potpora ne opada. Stranka ima stabilno, postojano i vjerno biračko tijelo koje se s njom poistovjećuje. Iako joj se stalno predviđa propast, uspjela se ukorijeniti na stranačkoj sceni i opstaje.

### Kadrovska stranka iz 19. stoljeća

Najveću slabost Mosta Žižić vidi u izostanku **teritorijalne dimenzije**. Most ima vrlo prepoznatljive i aktivne saborske zastupnike koji važne teme stavljaju na javni dnevni red. Upravo se zato, objašnjava, stranka ponaša kao tip stranke nastao u 19. stoljeću, kao **kadrovska stranka** koja počiva na prepoznatljivim zastupnicima. Nedostaje joj, međutim, teritorijalno širenje po Hrvatskoj, a sve je previše usmjereno na uže vodstvo. Unatoč tome, Žižić je smatra strankom s potencijalom, što potvrđuju i istraživanja javnog mnijenja.

### Moguće ponovno okupljanje s Marijom Selak Raspudić

Žižić iznosi i konkretnu prognozu. Nakon prošlih parlamentarnih izbora došlo je do raskola između uže jezgre Mosta i Marije Selak Raspudić. Strane su očito ostale u dobrim odnosima i stalno ističu da i dalje surađuju. Zato Žižić smatra da bi na sljedeće izbore, bili oni redoviti za godinu i pol ili ranije, mogli izaći u nekom obliku koalicije.

Stranka Drito, čiji naziv Žižić s dozom ironije opisuje kao **neinventivan**, nije se po njegovoj ocjeni nigdje proširila ni ukorijenila. Ako želi politički opstati, najbolje joj je udružiti se s Mostom. Budući da ima dobru bazu u Zagrebu, takvo bi okupljanje moglo koristiti objema stranama.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom iznosi političku analizu i ne zastupa tvrdnje koje bi očito bile protivne katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Pojmovi poput konzervativizma, demokršćanstva i suverenizma sami po sebi ne određuju katoličku usklađenost neke stranke; presudno je kako njezini stavovi služe ljudskom dostojanstvu i općem dobru.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički društveni nauk nije politička ideologija ni potvrda određene stranačke etikete, nego prosudba društvene stvarnosti u svjetlu vjere i moralnih načela. Zato se politička stranka ili koalicija može vrednovati prema konkretnim politikama, osobito prema zaštiti ljudskog života, obitelji, pravednosti i općeg dobra, a ne samo prema samoodređenju ili izbornom uspjehu.

sections.subtitle_en: Most: sovereignists fleeing ideological labels, while their electorate does not falter
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains why Most has a stable and faithful electorate despite constant predictions of doom
sections.content_en:
After the analysis of the left part of the spectrum, host **Marin Marić** moves on to the rest of the opposition. He recalls that Most crossed 10 percent of support and is increasingly present in the media. Nevertheless, very different ideological labels are attributed to the party: somewhere they are called conservatives, somewhere Christian Democrats, and somewhere the label of populism is pasted onto them. Recently, they have risen most on anti-corruption topics, so Marić asks what their essential ideology is.

Political scientist **Jakov Žižić** replies that Most consciously fled from ideological designations. He sees the reason in their rationality: they understand that such designations have a negative meaning in public. Žižić emphasizes that Most follows the mood of citizens well and has, as he says, good sensors for recognizing public opinion. In an ideological sense, especially when it comes to social values, the party is in his assessment **conservative**. The program contains many Christian democratic attributes, but Most would never call itself a Christian Democratic party. It speaks of itself as a **sovereignist party**.

Žižić highlights one interesting point: Most's voter support is not declining. The party has a stable, steadfast, and faithful electorate that identifies with it. Although doom is constantly predicted for it, it has managed to take root on the party scene and survives.

### A 19th-century cadre party

Žižić sees Most's greatest weakness in the lack of a **territorial dimension**. Most has very recognizable and active members of parliament who place important topics on the public agenda. Exactly because of this, he explains, the party behaves like a type of party originating in the 19th century, as a **cadre party** that rests on recognizable deputies. However, it lacks territorial expansion across Croatia, and everything is too focused on the narrow leadership. Despite this, Žižić considers it a party with potential, which is also confirmed by public opinion polls.

### Possible reunion with Marija Selak Raspudić

Žižić also offers a concrete forecast. After the last parliamentary elections, a rift occurred between the core of Most and Marija Selak Raspudić. The parties apparently remained on good terms and constantly emphasize that they still cooperate. Therefore, Žižić considers that in the next elections, whether regular in a year and a half or earlier, they could run in some form of coalition.

The party Drito, whose name Žižić describes with a dose of irony as **uninventive**, has in his assessment neither expanded nor taken root anywhere. If it wants to survive politically, its best move is to join forces with Most. Since it has a good base in Zagreb, such a gathering could benefit both sides.

sections.subtitle: Fokus i Republika: još jedan tehnokratski pokušaj i birači s laptopom koji ipak glasuju za Možemo
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić na primjeru javne ceste objašnjava zašto se tržišna logika ne može primijeniti na javne usluge
sections.content:
Marić spominje spajanje Fokusa i Republike i pita otvara li to prostor u političkom centru. Žižić je skeptičan. Smatra da je riječ o **još jednom tehnokratskom pokušaju** koji će birače uvjeravati u važnost stručnjaka i eksperata, u to da sve treba prepustiti kompetentnima i da u politici treba primijeniti logiku gospodarstva.

Podsjeća da je sve to već pokušao **Damir Vanđelić** 2024. godine, s rezultatima koje opisuje kao, blago rečeno, skromne. Ne vidi što bi takva opcija sada mogla ponuditi drugačije.

### Gdje završavaju hrvatski liberali

Žižić upozorava na strukturni problem takvih stranaka. Prema istraživanjima ideološkog svrstavanja, u Hrvatskoj postoji oko **20 posto liberala s protržišnim stavovima**, ali oni će prije glasovati za Možemo nego za neku izričito liberalnu stranku. Marić dodaje da dio njih glasuje i za HDZ. Žižić to prihvaća uz ogradu: za HDZ glasuju oni s katoličkom pozadinom i konzervativnim društvenim vrijednostima.

Nova srednja klasa, visokoobrazovani ljudi koji rade u ekonomiji znanja, odnosno **klasa s laptopom**, kako ih Žižić naziva, prema njegovu opisu ne voli regulacije i ograničenja. Ti se birači svugdje osjećaju kao doma, sputavaju ih nacionalne granice i identiteti, a po prirodi naginju **liberalnom individualizmu**. Takvi idu prema Možemo, a ne prema Vanđeliću i Fokusu, kako god se ta opcija na kraju zvala. Zato ona, zaključuje Žižić, ne može ništa napraviti: ne zna ponuditi nešto novo i drugačije.

### Štrajk kao lakmus-papir

Kao najbolji primjer Žižić ponovno navodi štrajk radnika Zagrebačkog holdinga i Čistoće. Liberalni dio javnosti tada je na kraju podržao zagrebačku gradsku vlast, uz argumente da su radnici neradnici i preplaćeni te da treba uvesti mjere učinkovitosti i kriterije iz privatnog sektora. Marić se nadovezuje opaskom o stranim radnicima.

Žižić se tome oštro suprotstavlja. U javne usluge ne mogu se unositi kriteriji privatnog sektora, jer su neke usluge preskupe da bi se financirale drugačije nego **solidarno i kolektivno**. Slikovito pita kako bi uopće došao do studija nekom privatnom cestom. Došao je javnom cestom koju svi zajedno financiraju. Isto vrijedi za sigurnost i zdravstvo: to su javna dobra i javne usluge u koje se ne može ugraditi tržišna logika kakvu takve opcije nameću. Dodaje da se na izborima vidi kako prolaze.

### Literatura čitana u vakuumu

Marić primjećuje da dio ljudi čita američku literaturu, primjerice Miltona Friedmana, izvan konteksta, uvjeren da se ona bez problema može presaditi u hrvatski, pa i katolički medijski prostor. Žižić to naziva **nerazumijevanjem ideologija**. Protržišna logika, ideja učinkovitosti i mjerenja te cijela liberalna tržišna logika neće se, prema njegovoj ocjeni, izraziti kroz Vanđelićevu ili Fokusovu stranku, kao ni kroz ranije pokušaje poput Zurovčeva. Takvi glasovi većinom idu Možemo, i upravo zato zasebna politička opcija te vrste ne uspijeva zaživjeti.

magisterium.assessment: Kritika svođenja javnih usluga na profit i tržišnu učinkovitost u skladu je s katoličkim naglaskom da gospodarstvo treba služiti ljudskoj osobi, solidarnosti i općem dobru. Ipak, tvrdnja da se kriteriji privatnog sektora uopće ne mogu primijeniti na javne usluge zvuči preširoko: katolički nauk upozorava na dominaciju profita, ali ne zabranjuje svaku tržišnu mjeru, privatnu inicijativu ili zahtjev za učinkovitom upravom.
concerns: Kategoričko odbacivanje tržišne logike u javnim uslugama može zamagliti razliku između profita kao jedinog mjerila i razborite uporabe mjerenja učinkovitosti, ako ona ne potiskuje dostojanstvo radnika ni dostupnost usluge.

Opisivanje skupina birača kao da ih jedinstveno određuju klasa, vrijednosti ili odnos prema regulaciji politički je pojednostavljen prikaz; sam po sebi nije teološka pogreška, ali ga ne treba uzimati kao moralnu procjenu pojedinaca.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne svodi gospodarstvo na izbor između neograničenog tržišta i potpunog odbacivanja tržišnih mehanizama: gospodarske odluke trebaju služiti čovjeku i zajedničkom dobru, uz solidarnost i supsidijarnost. Biblijski naglasak na dijeljenju i skrbi za siromašne podupire kritiku zanemarivanja potrebitih, dok ne daje osnovu za zaključak da je svako tržišno sredstvo samo po sebi neprihvatljivo.

magisterium.assessment_en: Criticism of reducing public services to profit and market efficiency aligns with the Catholic emphasis that the economy should serve the human person, solidarity, and the common good. However, the assertion that private sector criteria cannot be applied to public services at all sounds overly broad: Catholic teaching warns against the dominance of profit, but does not forbid every market measure, private initiative, or requirement for efficient administration.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not reduce the economy to a choice between an unrestricted market and the total rejection of market mechanisms: economic decisions should serve man and the common good, alongside solidarity and subsidiarity. The biblical emphasis on sharing and care for the poor supports the criticism of neglecting the needy, while providing no basis for concluding that every market tool is unacceptable in itself.
concerns_en: A categorical rejection of market logic in public services can blur the distinction between profit as the sole criterion and the prudent use of efficiency metrics, provided they do not suppress worker dignity or service accessibility.

Describing groups of voters as though they are uniformly determined by class, values, or attitude toward regulation is a politically simplified portrayal; in itself it is not a theological error, but it should not be taken as a moral assessment of individuals.

sections.subtitle_en: Fokus and Republika: yet another technocratic attempt and laptop voters who still vote for Možemo
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić uses the example of a public road to explain why market logic cannot be applied to public services
sections.content_en:
Marić mentions the merger of Fokus and Republika and asks whether that opens up space in the political center. Žižić is skeptical. He believes that this is **yet another technocratic attempt** that will convince voters of the importance of experts, that everything should be left to the competent, and that the logic of the economy should be applied in politics.

He recalls that all of this was already attempted by **Damir Vanđelić** in 2024, with results he describes as, mildly put, modest. He does not see what such an option could now offer differently.

### Where Croatian liberals end up

Žižić warns of the structural problem of such parties. According to research on ideological alignment, in Croatia there are about **20 percent of liberals with pro-market stances**, but they will sooner vote for Možemo than for an explicitly liberal party. Marić adds that part of them also vote for HDZ. Žižić accepts that with a caveat: those with a Catholic background and conservative social values vote for HDZ.

The new middle class, highly educated people who work in the knowledge economy, namely the **laptop class**, as Žižić calls them, according to his description do not like regulations and restrictions. These voters feel at home everywhere, national borders and identities restrain them, and by nature they lean toward **liberal individualism**. Such voters head toward Možemo, not toward Vanđelić and Fokus, whatever that option is ultimately called. That is why, Žižić concludes, it cannot accomplish anything: it does not know how to offer something new and different.

### The strike as a litmus test

As the best example, Žižić again cites the strike of workers of Zagrebački holding and Čistoća. The liberal part of the public then ultimately supported the Zagreb city government, with arguments that the workers are loafers and overpaid and that efficiency measures and criteria from the private sector should be introduced. Marić follows up with a remark about foreign workers.

Žižić sharply opposes this. Private-sector criteria cannot be introduced into public services, because some services are too expensive to be financed other than **solidarily and collectively**. Figuratively, he asks how he would have reached the studio at all via some private road. He arrived on a public road that everyone finances together. The same applies to security and healthcare: these are public goods and public services into which the market logic imposed by such options cannot be embedded. He adds that elections show how they fare.

### Literature read in a vacuum

Marić observes that some people read American literature, for example Milton Friedman, out of context, convinced that it can easily be transplanted into Croatian, and even Catholic, media space. Žižić calls this a **misunderstanding of ideologies**. Pro-market logic, the idea of efficiency and measurement, and the entire liberal market logic will not, in his assessment, be expressed through Vanđelić's or Fokus's party, nor through earlier attempts like Zurovec's. Such votes mostly go to Možemo, and that is precisely why a separate political option of that kind fails to take root.

sections.subtitle: Domovinski pokret i DOMiNO: od tvrde oporbe do koalicije s HDZ-om i raskola
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić opisuje kako je Domovinski pokret nakon izbora odmah ušao u koaliciju s HDZ-om koji je prije oštro napadao
sections.content:
Prelazeći na desnicu, Marić primjećuje da je ona to fragmentiranija što se ide dalje udesno. Kao predvodnike navodi Domovinski pokret (DP) i DOMiNO, odnosno cijelu Vukovarsku koaliciju. Žižić ga odmah ispravlja: Vukovarska koalicija **ne postoji**. Nazvana je tako prije više od godinu dana, a otad se taj pojam uopće ne pojavljuje u političkom diskursu.

Na pitanje o ideologiji dviju sukobljenih stranaka koje su nekad bile zajedno, Žižić je kratak: **ideologije tu nema**. Podsjeća da je Domovinski pokret pri osnivanju bio tvrda i oštra oporba HDZ-u i Andreju Plenkoviću. Optuživali su ga da je udaljio HDZ od izvornih postavki, nazivali ga slugom Bruxellesa i govorili da HDZ više nije suverenistička, državotvorna i domoljubna stranka, nego da se prodao Bruxellesu i srpskoj manjini. Čim su izbori završili, DP je ipak **odmah pohitao u koaliciju** s Plenkovićem i HDZ-om.

### Cijena ulaska u vlast

To je, objašnjava Žižić, izazvalo unutarnja trvenja. Neki su bili svjesni cijene takve koalicije, neki su htjeli izvući veću korist, a treći su smatrali da drugog izbora nema. Iz toga je proizašao raskol.

Šanse obiju opcija Žižić ocjenjuje kao **vrlo male**. DP se pokušava izboriti za političke pobjede, a HDZ, koji dobro upravlja odnosima s koalicijskim partnerima, daje mu prigode da se istakne u nekim politikama. Sve je to, međutim, slabo. Prema Žižiću, DP je izgubio Vukovar kao svoju bazu, pa će mu biti teško osvojiti i jedan do dva mandata u slavonskim izbornim jedinicama, gdje je najjači.

Zato vidi samo jedan siguran put opstanka. DP drži **tri vrlo važna resora**, i najbolje bi bilo da se njegovi ministri u njima dokažu Andreju Plenkoviću te da ih on stavi na listu HDZ-a. Marić to sažima riječju „najsigurnije“, a Žižić potvrđuje: samostalan izlazak na izbore jamči im možda jedan ili dva mandata.

### DOMiNO bez prostora za rast

Ni DOMiNO prema Žižićevoj procjeni nema prostora za rast. Ne može nastaviti raniju politiku DP-a iz vremena kad su bili zajedno, jer je HDZ odabrao **desniju koalicijsku fazu**: više nije u koaliciji sa SDSS-om ili centrističkim i regionalnim strankama, nego s DP-om. Zato DOMiNO mora smisliti kako opstati. Žižić tu najavljuje temu Igora Štimca, jer Hrvati, kako kaže, vole popularne figure, osobito sportske, a slava i prepoznatljivost iz sporta znaju se pretočiti u politiku.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak uglavnom iznosi političku analizu i ne zagovara izravno stav koji bi proturječio katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Ipak, opis političkog opstanka, ministarskih položaja i ulaska na stranačku listu gotovo isključivo kao strategije za očuvanje mandata može ostaviti dojam instrumentalnog shvaćanja politike, dok katolički nauk političko djelovanje prosuđuje prema služenju općem dobru.
concerns: Izraz da je najpouzdaniji put opstanka ministara da se dokažu predsjedniku Vlade i budu stavljeni na stranačku listu naglašava osobnu i stranačku korist; ako bi to bio cilj sam po sebi, bilo bi u napetosti s političkom odgovornošću usmjerenom na opće dobro. Budući da je riječ o analizi izbornog položaja, a ne nužno o odobravanju takva pristupa, to je ograničena primjedba, ne dokaz izravnog naukovnog proturječja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk dopušta laicima različite političke izbore, ali traži da oni budu ukorijenjeni u ljubavi i usmjereni na opće dobro; nijedna stranka ili koalicija ne može se poistovjetiti s cjelinom kršćanske vjere. Zato se koalicije i politički kompromisi mogu procjenjivati razborito, ali ne samo prema broju mandata ili očuvanju položaja: važni su i konkretni učinci na ljudsko dostojanstvo, pravednost, solidarnost i prava slabijih.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage mainly presents political analysis and does not directly advocate a position that would contradict Catholic teaching or Scripture. Still, describing political survival, ministerial posts, and joining a party list almost exclusively as a strategy for retaining seats can give the impression of an instrumental understanding of politics, whereas Catholic teaching judges political action by service to the common good.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching allows the laity diverse political choices, but requires that they be rooted in charity and directed toward the common good; no party or coalition can be equated with the entirety of the Christian faith. Therefore, coalitions and political compromises can be evaluated prudently, but not solely by the number of seats or preservation of positions: concrete effects on human dignity, justice, solidarity, and the rights of the weaker are also important.
concerns_en: The phrase that the most reliable path of survival for ministers is to prove themselves to the Prime Minister and be placed on the party list emphasizes personal and partisan gain; if this were an end in itself, it would be in tension with political responsibility directed toward the common good. Since this is an analysis of electoral positioning rather than necessarily an endorsement of such an approach, it is a limited observation, not evidence of a direct doctrinal contradiction.

sections.subtitle_en: Domovinski pokret and DOMiNO: from hard opposition to coalition with HDZ and a rift
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić describes how Domovinski pokret immediately after the elections entered into a coalition with HDZ, which it had previously sharply attacked
sections.content_en:
Moving on to the right, Marić observes that it is more fragmented the further right one goes. As leaders, he mentions Domovinski pokret (DP) and DOMiNO, that is, the entire Vukovar coalition. Žižić immediately corrects him: the Vukovar coalition **does not exist**. It was named so more than a year ago, and since then that term does not appear in political discourse at all.

To the question about the ideology of the two conflicting parties that once were together, Žižić is brief: **there is no ideology here**. He recalls that at its founding Domovinski pokret was a hard and sharp opposition to HDZ and Andrej Plenković. They accused him of having moved HDZ away from its original premises, called him a servant of Brussels, and said that HDZ was no longer a sovereignist, state-building, and patriotic party, but had sold out to Brussels and the Serbian minority. As soon as the elections ended, however, DP **immediately rushed into a coalition** with Plenković and HDZ.

### The price of entering government

That, Žižić explains, caused internal friction. Some were aware of the price of such a coalition, some wanted to extract greater benefit, and others believed there was no other choice. Out of that arose a rift.

Žižić assesses the chances of both options as **very small**. DP is trying to fight for political victories, and HDZ, which manages relations with coalition partners well, gives it opportunities to distinguish itself in some policies. All of that, however, is weak. According to Žižić, DP has lost Vukovar as its base, so it will be difficult for it to win even one to two mandates in Slavonian electoral units, where it is strongest.

Therefore, he sees only one certain path of survival. DP holds **three very important portfolios**, and it would be best for its ministers to prove themselves in them to Andrej Plenković and for him to put them on HDZ's list. Marić summarizes this with the word "safest," and Žižić confirms: running independently in the elections guarantees them perhaps one or two mandates.

### DOMiNO with no room for growth

DOMiNO, according to Žižić's assessment, has no room for growth either. It cannot continue the earlier policy of DP from the time when they were together, because HDZ chose a **more right-wing coalition phase**: it is no longer in coalition with SDSS or centrist and regional parties, but with DP. Therefore, DOMiNO must figure out how to survive. Žižić here announces the topic of Igor Štimac, because Croats, as he says, love popular figures, especially sports ones, and fame and recognizability from sports often translate into politics.

sections.subtitle: Suverenizam je nacionalizam, a ideološki moratorij stiže iz Poljske
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava da Hrvatska 35 godina ima nacionalnu državu i da sam nacionalizam više ne nudi sve odgovore
sections.content:
Marić pita gdje bi u podjeli na monističke i pluralističke ideologije smjestio suverenizam, koji baštini i Most. Žižić odgovara da **suverenizam nije zasebna ideologija, nego nacionalizam**. Budući da se nacionalizam često doživljava kao pogrdna etiketa, upotrebljava se drugi naziv. Riječ je o ideji važnosti nacionalnih država koje zadržavaju **upravljačke poluge**, pokušavaju upravljati ekonomskim i socijalnim politikama te se odupiru globalizaciji, liberalizaciji i deregulaciji.

Žižić naglašava da nacionalizam promatra vrijednosno neutralno, kao legitimnu političku ideologiju s velikim mobilizacijskim nabojem, a ne kao pogrdan pojam. Ipak, upozorava na njegovo ograničenje. Nacionalizam je prvenstveno vezan uz nacije koje se još nisu konstituirale u vlastitu državu. Hrvati nacionalnu državu imaju već **35 godina** i više nisu nacija bez države, pa pred njima stoje druge teme i prioriteti.

To ne znači da ideja suverene nacionalne države nije važna. Žižić podsjeća da se u nizu situacija pokazalo koliko je bitno zadržati upravljačke poluge, sam odlučivati i uspostavljati red u vlastitoj državi. Ali nacionalizam sam po sebi ne daje odgovore na mnoga važna društvena i politička pitanja.

### Preporuka: demokršćanstvo s jasnom antropologijom

Zato Žižić smatra da je bolje profilirati se unutar neke od pluralističkih ideologija. Predlaže neki oblik **demokršćanstva**, ali ne suvremenog, koje je jako sekularizirano i u antropološkom smislu postalo liberalno. Riječ bi bila o demokršćanstvu s **jasnom kršćanskom antropologijom** i jasnom idejom suverene nacionalne države koja i dalje vodi aktivnu ekonomsku i socijalnu politiku.

### Ideološki moratorij i poljska lekcija

Prije prelaska na izborne kombinacije Marić otvara pojam **ideološkog moratorija**. Žižić navodi da je u hrvatskom kontekstu riječ o kovanici Nina Raspudića, ali da je ideja izvorno potekla iz Poljske, a Marić dodaje i Mađarsku. U Poljskoj se, objašnjava Žižić, ideja konkretno pretočila u praksu: opcija vrlo slična Mostu nakon izbora nije odabrala nacionalno-konzervativnu stranku Pravo i pravda, nego liberalnu, lijevo-centrističku opciju oko Tuska. Ideja da se o nekim temama jednostavno neće govoriti, upozorava Žižić, u praksi je vrlo teško provediti. Marić zaključuje da će se to vidjeti na izborima i nakon njih.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak prepoznaje legitimnu važnost suverene države i pozitivno ističe demokršćanstvo oblikovano jasnom kršćanskom antropologijom, što se može uskladiti s katoličkim društvenim naukom. No tvrdnja da je nacionalizam vrijednosno neutralan i da je zapravo drugo ime za suverenizam preširoka je u svjetlu crkvenog razlikovanja legitimnog domoljublja od nacionalizma obilježenog prezirom ili neprijateljstvom prema drugim narodima, a ideološki moratorij ne bi smio značiti šutnju o temeljnim moralnim pitanjima.
concerns: Crkveni izvor razlikuje domoljublje—legitimnu, ali ne isključivu ljubav i služenje vlastitoj zemlji—od nacionalizma koji uključuje prezir ili čak mržnju prema drugim narodima i kulturama; zato se nacionalizam ne može bez ograničenja prikazati kao vrijednosno neutralan. Suverenitet i upravljačke ovlasti države mogu biti legitimna politička dobra, ali sami po sebi ne određuju je li neki nacionalni program pravedan.

Ideološki moratorij može biti taktički dogovor o redoslijedu ili opsegu rasprave, ali postaje problematičan ako znači odustajanje od svjedočenja o neiznimnim moralnim pitanjima ili prihvaćanje da se temeljne istine prešućuju radi političke suradnje. Katolički nauk dopušta djelovanje s drugima, ali ne dopušta kompromitiranje temeljnih moralnih načela.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko društveno učenje drži zajedno posebnu odgovornost prema vlastitoj zajednici i dužnosti prema drugim narodima i cijelom čovječanstvu: nacionalna kultura i pravo naroda na vlastito postojanje ne ukidaju obvezu mira, poštovanja i solidarnosti. Kršćanska politička vizija zato ne mora birati između nacionalne samostalnosti i univerzalne moralne odgovornosti; suverenitet treba prosuđivati prema tome služi li ljudskoj osobi i općem dobru. U dostavljenim odlomcima nema izravnog tumačenja biblijskog teksta, pa se biblijska usklađenost može procijeniti samo posredno, kroz te katoličke kriterije istine, pravednosti i ljubavi prema bližnjemu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage recognizes the legitimate importance of a sovereign state and positively highlights Christian democracy shaped by a clear Christian anthropology, which can be aligned with Catholic social teaching. But the assertion that nationalism is value-neutral and is actually another name for sovereignism is overly broad in light of the Church's distinction between legitimate patriotism and nationalism marked by contempt or hostility toward other nations, and an ideological moratorium should not mean silence on fundamental moral issues.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic social teaching holds together special responsibility toward one's own community and duties toward other nations and the whole of humanity: national culture and the right of nations to their own existence do not abolish the obligations of peace, respect, and solidarity. A Christian political vision therefore does not have to choose between national independence and universal moral responsibility; sovereignty must be judged according to whether it serves the human person and the common good. In the provided passages there is no direct interpretation of a biblical text, so biblical alignment can be evaluated only indirectly, through these Catholic criteria of truth, justice, and love of neighbor.
concerns_en: Church sources distinguish patriotism—legitimate, but not exclusive love and service to one's own country—from nationalism that involves contempt or even hatred toward other nations and cultures; therefore, nationalism cannot be portrayed unconditionally as value-neutral. State sovereignty and administrative powers can be legitimate political goods, but in themselves they do not determine whether a national program is just.

An ideological moratorium can be a tactical agreement on the order or scope of debate, but it becomes problematic if it means abandoning witness on non-negotiable moral issues or accepting that fundamental truths be silenced for the sake of political cooperation. Catholic teaching permits working with others, but does not allow compromising fundamental moral principles.

sections.subtitle_en: Sovereignism is nationalism, and the ideological moratorium comes from Poland
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains that Croatia has had a nation-state for 35 years and that nationalism alone no longer offers all the answers
sections.content_en:
Marić asks where in the division between monistic and pluralistic ideologies he would place sovereignism, which Most also inherits. Žižić replies that **sovereignism is not a separate ideology, but nationalism**. Since nationalism is often perceived as a pejorative label, another name is used. It is about the idea of the importance of nation-states that retain **steering levers**, try to manage economic and social policies, and resist globalization, liberalization, and deregulation.

Žižić emphasizes that he views nationalism in a value-neutral way, as a legitimate political ideology with great mobilizing charge, not as a pejorative concept. However, he warns of its limitation. Nationalism is primarily tied to nations that have not yet constituted themselves into their own state. Croats have had a nation-state for **35 years** already and are no longer a nation without a state, so different topics and priorities stand before them.

That does not mean that the idea of a sovereign nation-state is not important. Žižić recalls that in a series of situations it proved how vital it is to retain steering levers, make decisions independently, and establish order in one's own state. But nationalism in itself does not provide answers to many important social and political questions.

### Recommendation: Christian democracy with a clear anthropology

Therefore, Žižić considers it better to profile oneself within one of the pluralistic ideologies. He suggests some form of **Christian democracy**, but not contemporary, which is heavily secularized and in an anthropological sense has become liberal. It would be Christian democracy with a **clear Christian anthropology** and a clear idea of a sovereign nation-state that continues to lead active economic and social policy.

### Ideological moratorium and the Polish lesson

Before moving on to electoral combinations, Marić opens the concept of an **ideological moratorium**. Žižić states that in the Croatian context it is a coinage of Nino Raspudić, but that the idea originally originated in Poland, and Marić adds Hungary as well. In Poland, Žižić explains, the idea was concretely translated into practice: an option very similar to Most after the elections did not choose the national-conservative party Law and Justice, but the liberal, center-left option around Tusk. The idea that certain topics simply will not be discussed, Žižić warns, is very difficult to implement in practice. Marić concludes that this will be seen in the elections and after them.

sections.subtitle: Politička egokracija: Plenković, Milanović i sustav koji proizvodi sukobe
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava pojam političke egokracije i sukob Andreja Plenkovića i Zorana Milanovića
sections.content:
Marić se poziva na Žižićevu kolumnu o još jednoj, kako je naziva, takozvanoj ideologiji vrlo prisutnoj u Hrvatskoj: **egokraciji**. Riječ je o dominaciji političkih osobnosti nad ideologijama, osobito na samom vrhu vlasti. Pita koliko je to naštetilo hrvatskom političkom prostoru.

Žižić objašnjava da je pojam **politička egokracija** sam plasirao. Opisuje njime dominaciju dviju snažnih političkih osobnosti, **Andreja Plenkovića** i **Zorana Milanovića**, koji su po njegovu mišljenju i svjesno odabrali međusobni sukob i sporenje. Hrvatska je tako ušla u fazu vladavine dvaju političkih ega.

Trenutačno je, procjenjuje Žižić, mirna faza bez eskalacije, a predsjednik je prilično politički uspavan. Ako se nešto dogodi, probudit će se. Ne isključuje ni da Milanović djeluje u pozadini, posebno kad je riječ o SDP-u.

### Korijeni u ustavnoj promjeni iz 2000.

Žižić upozorava da problem nije samo u osobnostima nego i u institucijama. Kad je 2000. mijenjan **polupredsjednički sustav**, predsjednik je bio popularni Mesić, pa mu je ostavljen dio izvršnih ovlasti umjesto da postane ceremonijalna figura. Da je tada pobijedio HDZ-ov kandidat Mate Granić, tadašnja bi vlast, smatra Žižić, predsjednika realno pretvorila u ceremonijalnu figuru. Rezultat je današnje stanje: težište izvršne moći je u Vladi, odnosno kod predsjednika Vlade, ali predsjednik Republike zadržava određene ovlasti i utjecaj. Kad se na tim mjestima nađu dva snažna ega, sukob je neizbježan, a obojici se politički isplati.

Na Marićevo pitanje je li dakle kriv i sam ustroj institucija, Žižić odgovara potvrdno. Konfiguracija je vrlo važna jer im daje kontekst. Da je Milanović predsjednik bez ovlasti, mogao bi se svađati, ali ne bi mogao, primjerice, blokirati odlazak počasne postrojbe u Pariz. Marić primjećuje da je to bio jedan od rijetkih pravih institucionalnih sporova. Žižić nabraja još:

- sukob oko **imenovanja predsjednika Vrhovnog suda**, kojeg predsjednik predlaže, a Sabor potvrđuje;
- **veleposlanike** koje Hrvatska godinama nema jer se dvojica moraju dogovoriti;
- krize oko imenovanja **čelnika sigurnosnih službi**.

Zaključuje da problemi nastaju gdje god se ovlasti dijele, odnosno gdje god predsjednik ima utjecaj.

### Institucionalni konzervatizam

Kad Marić upita bi li bilo bolje da je sve u rukama jednoga, Žižić naglašava da to nije rekao. Pita se, međutim, zašto se ne bi razmišljalo o nekoj reformi. U Hrvatskoj se, ističe, o tome ne smije ništa reći: ne može se mijenjati model izbora ustavnih sudaca, izborni sustav ni politički sustav. Marić to opisuje kao da je uklesano u kamen, a Žižić to naziva **institucionalnim konzervatizmom**. Na Marićevu opasku o pritisku viših instanci odgovara da takav pritisak izvana prije ide u smjeru ekonomske liberalizacije i deregulacije nego institucionalnih reformi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim društvenim naukom: kritika osobne dominacije i institucionalnih blokada može se razumjeti kao briga za vlast koja služi općem dobru, a ne samovolji pojedinaca. Pozitivno je i što se reforma razmatra bez tvrdnje da svu vlast treba predati jednoj osobi; katolički nauk izričito priznaje vrijednost podjele i međusobnog uravnoteženja vlasti.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je sukob dvaju nositelja vlasti „neizbježan” politička je procjena, a ne teološki zaključak; kršćanski pogled ne svodi političko ponašanje na neizbježan učinak institucija, nego uzima u obzir i osobnu odgovornost, savjest i mogućnost djelovanja za opće dobro.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne propisuje jedan obvezan ustavni model, nego vrednuje institucije prema tome štite li dostojanstvo osoba, pravnu odgovornost i opće dobro; podjela vlasti služi tome da zakon, a ne samovoljna volja pojedinca, bude mjerodavan. Biblijsko poštovanje civilne vlasti ne znači odobravanje svakog njezina čina: njezino je služenje vrijedno kada se vrši pravedno i unutar vlastitih granica.
