magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic social teaching: criticism of personal dominance and institutional gridlock can be understood as concern for governance serving the common good rather than individual arbitrariness. It is also positive that reform is considered without asserting that all power should be surrendered to a single person; Catholic teaching explicitly recognizes the value of the separation and mutual balancing of powers.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not prescribe a single mandatory constitutional model, but evaluates institutions according to whether they protect the dignity of persons, legal accountability, and the common good; the separation of powers ensures that the law, rather than the arbitrary will of an individual, is authoritative. Biblical respect for civil authority does not mean endorsing every act of authority: its service is valuable when exercised justly and within its proper limits.
concerns_en: The assertion that conflict between two officeholders is "inevitable" is a political assessment, not a theological conclusion; the Christian view does not reduce political behavior to an inevitable outcome of institutions, but also takes into account personal responsibility, conscience, and the possibility of acting for the common good.

sections.subtitle_en: Political egocracy: Plenković, Milanović, and the system that produces conflicts
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains the concept of political egocracy and the conflict between Andrej Plenković and Zoran Milanović
sections.content_en:
Marić refers to Žižić's column about yet another, as he calls it, so-called ideology very present in Croatia: **egocracy**. It is about the dominance of political personalities over ideologies, especially at the very top of government. He asks how much that has damaged the Croatian political arena.

Žižić explains that he launched the term **political egocracy** himself. With it he describes the dominance of two strong political personalities, **Andrej Plenković** and **Zoran Milanović**, who in his opinion also consciously chose mutual conflict and dispute. Croatia has thus entered a phase of rule by two political egos.

Currently, Žižić assesses, it is a calm phase without escalation, and the president is quite politically dormant. If something happens, he will wake up. He does not rule out that Milanović acts in the background, especially when it comes to SDP.

### Roots in the constitutional change of 2000

Žižić warns that the problem is not only in personalities but also in institutions. When the **semi-presidential system** was changed in 2000, the president was the popular Mesić, so he was left with part of executive powers instead of becoming a ceremonial figure. If HDZ candidate Mate Granić had won then, the government of that time, Žižić believes, would have realistically turned the president into a ceremonial figure. The result is today's state: the center of gravity of executive power is in the Government, namely with the Prime Minister, but the President of the Republic retains certain powers and influence. When two strong egos find themselves in these positions, conflict is inevitable, and it pays off politically for both.

To Marić's question whether the setup of institutions itself is therefore to blame, Žižić answers affirmatively. Configuration is very important because it provides them with context. If Milanović were a president without powers, he could argue, but he would not be able, for example, to block the departure of the honor guard to Paris. Marić observes that this was one of the few real institutional disputes. Žižić lists more:

- the conflict over the **appointment of the President of the Supreme Court**, whom the president proposes and the Parliament confirms;
- **ambassadors** that Croatia has not had for years because the two must reach an agreement;
- crises over the appointment of **heads of security services**.

He concludes that problems arise wherever powers are shared, that is, wherever the president has influence.

### Institutional conservatism

When Marić asks whether it would be better if everything were in the hands of one person, Žižić emphasizes that he did not say that. He wonders, however, why one would not think about some reform. In Croatia, he points out, nothing may be said about that: the model of electing constitutional judges, the electoral system, nor the political system can be changed. Marić describes it as carved in stone, and Žižić calls it **institutional conservatism**. To Marić's remark about pressure from higher instances, he replies that such outside pressure rather goes in the direction of economic liberalization and deregulation than institutional reforms.

sections.subtitle: SDP i Možemo: koalicija je sigurna, ali tko će biti premijer?
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava zašto je Tomislav Tomašević najprihvatljiviji kandidat lijevog bloka
sections.content:
Nakon ideološke analize Marić prelazi na političke kalkulacije uz najavu da će se za godinu i pol ponovno sastati i provjeriti što se od prognoza ostvarilo. Prva veća najavljena koalicija je ona **SDP-a i Možemo**, pa pita tko će u njoj biti glavni.

Žižić navodi da obje stranke tvrde kako je koalicija sigurna, ali još nisu dogovorile tko bi bio njihov predsjednik Vlade ako osvoje većinu. Usput ispravlja čestu pogrešku: u Hrvatskoj se ne bira kandidat za premijera, jer premijera neposredno ne biramo. To je kratko pokušao jedino Izrael.

Razlog neodlučnosti Žižić vidi u tome što su i u Možemo i u SDP-u svjesni **slabosti predsjednika SDP-a Siniše Hajdaša Dončića**. Kao predsjednik veće stranke on bi bio prirodan izbor, ali s druge strane svjedočimo **velikom uzdizanju Tomislava Tomaševića**. Njega se, kaže Žižić, doživljava kao vrlo prepoznatljivog i jasnog po pitanju politika, vladanja i programa, što se za Hajdaša Dončića ne može reći.

### Tomaševićeva širina

Žižić naglašava da Tomašević nikad nije rekao da ima ambicije. Podsjeća, međutim, da je ranije govorio kako sigurno neće na treći mandat, a sada se treći mandat za gradonačelnika Zagreba ipak spominje. Marić dodaje da je ranije govorio i o povlačenju nakon dva mandata.

Od svih njih Tomašević je, po Žižićevoj ocjeni, **najprihvatljiviji, najuključiviji i najšire može doprijeti**. Kao ilustraciju navodi da Tomašević u najbližoj obitelji ima više katoličkih svećenika nego bilo koji demokršćanski političar ili političar koji se deklarira kao katolički. Marić dodaje da ima i rodbinu na desnici. Žižić odmah ističe da to ništa ne govori o njegovim stavovima: Tomašević je liberal i slijedi liberalnu, a ne kršćansku antropologiju. Ali to pokazuje njegov doseg. Godine 2024. došao je i na Sinjsku noć, što ne bi mogli ni Sandra Benčić, ni Ivana Kekin, ni Siniša Hajdaš Dončić. Ne zato što ne bi bili dobrodošli, nego zato što ne mogu tako široko zahvatiti. Tomašević je, navodi Žižić, **treći najpozitivniji političar u Hrvatskoj**, dok Hajdaša Dončića prema nekim istraživanjima nema ni među prvih deset.

### Razlika se smanjuje

Marić podsjeća da je iz Možemo poručeno kako će kandidata dati jača stranka, a to je trenutačno SDP. Žižić odgovara da se razlika stalno smanjuje i prema novom istraživanju iznosi četiri do pet postotnih bodova. Pravilo koje je izrekao Tomašević dakle stoji, ali SDP je u **nezaustavljivom padu**. Možemo je i dalje regionalna stranka usmjerena na Zagreb, no vladanje glavnim gradom daje joj veliku prepoznatljivost, prisutnost i moć.

Mogućnost da SDP da premijerskog kandidata, a Tomašević kandidira za predsjednika Republike, Žižić smatra malo vjerojatnom. Za takvu kandidaturu tražit će se iskustvo koje Tomašević još nema. Prirodan slijed nakon gradonačelničke funkcije u jedinoj metropoli zemlje jest ozbiljna izvršna vlast, a to je Vlada, a ne Pantovčak. Uz ogradu da politika ostaje nepredvidljiva, Žižić procjenjuje da rijetko tko i u SDP-u i u Možemo vidi Hajdaša Dončića kao premijera. Priče da Milanović već ima spremnog kandidata naziva **klišejima** i smatra izglednijim da se stranke na kraju odluče za najpopularnijeg i najprihvatljivijeg kandidata, Tomislava Tomaševića.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je pretežno politička analiza koalicijskih izgleda i popularnosti, pa sam po sebi ne proturječi katoličkom nauku; sudjelovanje građana i stranaka u demokratskom životu može biti legitimno usmjereno na opće dobro. Razlikovanje liberalne i kršćanske antropologije može biti teološki relevantno, ali bez objašnjenja što se pod tim pojmovima misli ostaje nedovoljno određeno za čvršću ocjenu.
concerns: Izraz „liberalna antropologija” širok je i višeznačan; bez navođenja konkretnih stavova ne treba zaključiti da je svaki liberalni politički položaj nužno suprotan kršćanskom shvaćanju čovjeka.

Obiteljske veze s katoličkim svećenicima i dolazak na javno okupljanje mogu ilustrirati društveni doseg, ali sami po sebi ne dokazuju političku ili antropološku usklađenost s katoličkim naukom; odlomak ipak izričito upozorava da rodbinske veze ne određuju nečije stavove.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko sudjelovanje u demokraciji ne zahtijeva poistovjećivanje Crkve s jednom strankom: vjernici trebaju oblikovati javni život kršćanskom savješću, štiteći ljudski život, pravdu, mir i opće dobro, uz suradnju s drugim građanima. Zato bi teološki sadržajnija procjena izraza „liberalna antropologija” trebala razmotriti konkretne tvrdnje o ljudskom dostojanstvu, slobodi, obitelji i moralnom dobru, a ne oslanjati se samo na stranačku oznaku.

citations.document_title: The Participation of Catholics in Political Life
citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is predominantly a political analysis of coalition prospects and popularity, and thus in itself does not contradict Catholic teaching; the participation of citizens and parties in democratic life can legitimately be directed toward the common good. Distinguishing liberal from Christian anthropology can be theologically relevant, but without explaining what is meant by these terms, it remains insufficiently defined for a firmer assessment.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic participation in democracy does not require equating the Church with a single party: believers must shape public life with a Christian conscience, protecting human life, justice, peace, and the common good, in cooperation with other citizens. Therefore, a theologically more substantial evaluation of the phrase "liberal anthropology" should consider concrete claims about human dignity, freedom, family, and the moral good, rather than relying solely on a party label.
concerns_en: The phrase "liberal anthropology" is broad and polysemous; without citing specific stances, one should not conclude that every liberal political position is necessarily contrary to the Christian understanding of man.

Family ties with Catholic priests and attending a public gathering may illustrate social reach, but in themselves do not prove political or anthropological alignment with Catholic teaching; the passage nevertheless explicitly warns that family ties do not determine one's views.

sections.subtitle_en: SDP and Možemo: a coalition is certain, but who will be prime minister?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains why Tomislav Tomašević is the most acceptable candidate of the left bloc
sections.content_en:
After the ideological analysis, Marić moves on to political calculations with the announcement that they will meet again in a year and a half and check which of the predictions came true. The first major announced coalition is that of **SDP and Možemo**, so he asks who will be the main one in it.

Žižić states that both parties claim the coalition is certain, but they have not yet agreed on who would be their Prime Minister if they win a majority. In passing, he corrects a common mistake: in Croatia a prime ministerial candidate is not elected, because we do not elect the prime minister directly. Only Israel attempted that briefly.

Žižić sees the reason for indecisiveness in the fact that both in Možemo and in SDP they are aware of the **weakness of SDP president Siniša Hajdaš Dončić**. As the president of the larger party, he would be the natural choice, but on the other hand we are witnessing the **great rise of Tomislav Tomašević**. He, says Žižić, is perceived as very recognizable and clear regarding policies, governance, and programs, which cannot be said for Hajdaš Dončić.

### Tomašević's breadth

Žižić emphasizes that Tomašević never said he has ambitions. He recalls, however, that he previously said he certainly would not run for a third term, yet now a third term as mayor of Zagreb is nevertheless mentioned. Marić adds that he previously spoke of stepping down after two terms as well.

Of all of them, Tomašević is, in Žižić's assessment, **the most acceptable, the most inclusive, and can reach out the broadest**. As an illustration, he states that Tomašević has more Catholic priests in his immediate family than any Christian democratic politician or politician who declares themselves Catholic. Marić adds that he also has relatives on the right. Žižić immediately emphasizes that this says nothing about his views: Tomašević is a liberal and follows liberal, not Christian anthropology. But that shows his reach. In 2024, he also came to Sinjska noć, which neither Sandra Benčić, nor Ivana Kekin, nor Siniša Hajdaš Dončić could do. Not because they would not be welcome, but because they cannot encompass so broadly. Tomašević is, states Žižić, **the third most positive politician in Croatia**, while Hajdaš Dončić, according to some polls, is not even among the top ten.

### The gap is narrowing

Marić recalls that Možemo communicated that the candidate would be provided by the stronger party, and that is currently SDP. Žižić replies that the difference is constantly narrowing and, according to a new poll, stands at four to five percentage points. The rule stated by Tomašević therefore stands, but SDP is in **an unstoppable decline**. Možemo is still a regional party focused on Zagreb, but governing the capital gives it great recognizability, presence, and power.

The possibility of SDP providing the prime ministerial candidate while Tomašević runs for President of the Republic, Žižić considers unlikely. For such a candidacy, experience that Tomašević does not yet have will be sought. The natural progression after mayoral office in the country's only metropolis is serious executive power, and that is the Government, not Pantovčak. With the caveat that politics remains unpredictable, Žižić assesses that hardly anyone in either SDP or Možemo sees Hajdaš Dončić as prime minister. He calls stories that Milanović already has a candidate ready **clichés** and considers it more likely that the parties in the end decide on the most popular and most acceptable candidate, Tomislav Tomašević.

sections.subtitle: Milanović i Hrvati u BiH: zašto se SDP nije usudio izaći iz vlastitih okvira
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava kako je Milanović iskoračio iz uskih okvira SDP-a po pitanju Hrvata u BiH
sections.content:
Marić podsjeća da je Milanović već jednom intervenirao u izbore i da to za SDP nije dobro završilo. Žižić odgovara da je Milanović tada **kandidirao sebe**, što je bitno drugačija situacija. Mogućnost da Milanović izađe s vlastitom listom i potom uđe u postizbornu koaliciju Žižić odbacuje kao nagađanje. Smatra da bi mu to bilo previše posla.

Na Marićevu tezu da se Milanović dodvoravao desnom dijelu biračkog spektra Žižić odgovara niječno. Milanović se, po njegovu mišljenju, nije dodvoravao, nego je iznosio stavove bitno drugačije od SDP-ovih i stavova Možemo, jer je shvatio da se ne može ostati ukopan u pozicijama u kojima je SDP.

### Propuštena prilika socijaldemokrata

Žižić postavlja retoričko pitanje: što je SDP-u, kao stranci koja se deklarira kao socijaldemokratska i koja se zauzima za marginalizirane, smetalo da u zaštitu uzme **Hrvate u Bosni i Hercegovini**? Ništa, odgovara, i stranka se tome mogla otvoriti. Milanović je to vidio i učinio, jer je znao izaći iz uskih okvira u kojima je i sam bio.

Žižić podsjeća da je Milanović u svojoj oportunističkoj fazi išao i na Komšićeve skupove, ali je na kraju shvatio što se događa u Bosni i Hercegovini. Socijaldemokratska partija mogla je, kaže, reći da staje u obranu jedne marginalizirane skupine, a Hrvati u BiH to su dobrim dijelom bili. Sve do Schmidta, ističe Žižić, pokušavalo ih se politički marginalizirati u vlastitoj domovini.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na zaštiti Hrvata u BiH kao moguće politički marginalizirane skupine načelno je usklađen s katoličkom solidarnošću i posebnom brigom za ranjive, bez obzira na njihovu nacionalnost. Ipak, odlomak iznosi široku političku ocjenu bez dovoljno pojedinosti da bi se procijenilo jesu li tvrdnje o marginalizaciji i ulozi Schmidta točne ili cjelovite.
concerns: Zaštita određene nacionalne skupine ne bi smjela postati isključivi nacionalizam niti zanemariti dostojanstvo i prava drugih skupina u BiH.
Opis političke marginalizacije iznesen je kao tvrdnja komentatora; katoličko načelo pravednosti traži činjeničnu i nepristranu procjenu konkretnih nepravdi.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk poziva na solidarnost preko nacionalnih, etničkih i ideoloških razlika te daje prvenstvenu pozornost slabima i ranjivima, pa je obrana Hrvata u BiH opravdana ako odgovara stvarnim nepravdama i služi općem dobru. Biblijski poziv na odgovornost za „najmanje“ podupire takvu brigu, ali zahtijeva da ona ne isključuje druge koji su također ugroženi.

citations.document_author: United States Conference of Catholic Bishops

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on protecting Croats in BiH as a potentially politically marginalized group is in principle aligned with Catholic solidarity and preferential concern for the vulnerable, regardless of their nationality. Nevertheless, the passage presents a broad political evaluation without sufficient detail to assess whether the claims of marginalization and Schmidt's role are accurate or complete.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching calls for solidarity across national, ethnic, and ideological lines and gives priority attention to the weak and vulnerable, so defending Croats in BiH is justified if it responds to real injustices and serves the common good. The biblical call to care for the "least of these" supports such concern, but requires that it not exclude others who are also endangered.
concerns_en: Protecting a specific national group should not become exclusive nationalism or disregard the dignity and rights of other groups in BiH.
The description of political marginalization is presented as an assertion of commentators; the Catholic principle of justice demands a factual and impartial evaluation of concrete injustices.

sections.subtitle_en: Milanović and Croats in BiH: why the SDP did not dare to step outside its own framework
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains how Milanović stepped outside the narrow framework of the SDP regarding the issue of Croats in BiH
sections.content_en:
Marić recalls that Milanović had already intervened in elections once and that it did not end well for the SDP. Žižić responds that Milanović then **candidated himself**, which is a significantly different situation. The possibility that Milanović runs with his own list and then enters a post-election coalition Žižić dismisses as speculation. He believes that would be too much work for him.

To Marić's thesis that Milanović was currying favor with the right-wing portion of the voter spectrum, Žižić responds in the negative. Milanović, in his opinion, was not currying favor, but was presenting stances significantly different from those of the SDP and Možemo, because he realized that one cannot remain entrenched in the positions the SDP is in.

### A missed opportunity for the social democrats

Žižić asks a rhetorical question: what prevented the SDP, as a party that declares itself social democratic and stands up for the marginalized, from taking **Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina** under its protection? Nothing, he answers, and the party could have opened up to it. Milanović saw this and did it, because he knew how to step outside the narrow framework in which he himself had been.

Žižić recalls that Milanović, in his opportunistic phase, even attended Komšić's rallies, but eventually realized what was happening in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Social Democratic Party could have, he says, stated that it was standing in defense of a marginalized group, and the Croats in BiH largely were that. Up until Schmidt, Žižić points out, attempts were made to politically marginalize them in their own homeland.

sections.subtitle: Igor Štimac: drski nogometaš kao mogući ujedinitelj desnice
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić opisuje kako Igor Štimac može pretočiti nogometnu drskost u politički kapital
sections.content:
Marić otvara temu **Igora Štimca**, koji se deklarirao kao budući ujedinitelj desnice, i pita po čemu bi se njegov projekt ideološki razlikovao od Mosta i Domovinskog pokreta, odnosno bi li bio nadideološko okupljanje.

Žižić podsjeća da je Štimac imao nekoliko nastupa u utjecajnim desnim medijskim kanalima: u jednom vrlo utjecajnom podcastu i u emisiji jednog utjecajnog desnog aktivista. U podcastu je rekao da ulazak u politiku još nije odlučen, a u drugoj emisiji da sigurno ulazi. Nakon toga ga više nema u medijima, pa Žižić smatra da ništa još nije sigurno.

### Grubost kao politički kapital

Štimac, objašnjava Žižić, može iskoristiti svoju prepoznatljivost, gard, grubost i drskost. On je pojam **drskog, grubog nogometaša** koji je na terenu ujedno i frajer. To se danas u politici traži: grubost, drskost i bezobraznost, osobito na društvenim mrežama. Zato to može pretočiti u politički kapital.

Problem je **financijski kapital**. Tko će sve to financirati i dati infrastrukturu? Infrastrukturu na desnici, osim HDZ-a, prema Žižiću ima jedino Most, a Most neće ići s njim jer je na 10 posto i Štimac mu ne treba. Štimac bi stoga trebao okupiti rascjepkane, usitnjene opcije. O DP-u, Penavi i Dabri izražava se dosta povoljno, a vidljivo je i da je blizak DOMiNU. Tu su i marginalne pravaške opcije, suverenisti i nestranački pojedinci. Potencijala ima, naglašava Žižić, ali otvoreno je pitanje novca i infrastrukture.

### Iskren prema HDZ-u

Najviše obećava, po Žižiću, Štimčeva jasna poruka: **„Mi želimo spasiti HDZ od poraza“**, uz otvoreno priznanje da je HDZ njihov prirodni koalicijski partner. U tome je iskreniji od nekih drugih opcija. Zasad se vide tek obrisi njegove političke opcije. Štimac je nezadovoljan smjerom HDZ-a i Hrvatske, ali tu je da HDZ promijeni. Drugima to nije uspijevalo, a on bi, zbog svog stava i habitusa čvrstog garda, mogao realno biti **ravnopravan HDZ-u** u potencijalnoj vlasti u koju bi ušao kako bi, po vlastitoj logici, spasio Hrvatsku od vlasti SDSS-a, Možemo i SDP-a.

Žižić upozorava i na tamniju stranu tog potencijala. Postoji desno biračko tijelo nezadovoljno HDZ-om koje se lako može zavesti pričama o **izgubljenoj Hrvatskoj** i o tome kako su na vlasti opet Jugoslaveni i Srbi. U tome se, kaže, mogu iskoristiti, pa i zloupotrijebiti nacionalni ideali, težnje, frustracije i traume ljudi. Ipak, ponovno pitajući tko će to financirati, zaključuje da je takav projekt vjerojatno **jedina opcija** da usitnjene stranke koje stoje na oko 2 posto nešto naprave.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak upozorava na moguću zloupotrebu nacionalnih frustracija i stoga prepoznaje stvaran moralni rizik, ali istodobno grubost i drskost prikazuje kao politički kapital bez jasnog odmaka od takve taktike. Posebno je potrebno razlikovati opis političke strategije od njezina odobravanja te odbaciti kolektivno optuživanje Srba ili drugih skupina.
concerns: Pretvaranje grubosti, bezobrazluka i drskosti u političku prednost napeto je s kršćanskim zahtjevom za ljubavlju, pravednošću i građanskim govorom.

Priče o „izgubljenoj Hrvatskoj“ i vlasti „Jugoslavena i Srba“ mogu poticati strah, predrasude ili neprijateljstvo prema čitavim skupinama; upozorenje na njihovu zloupotrebu jest važno, ali odlomak ne razrađuje dovoljno kako izbjeći takvu štetu.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko sudjelovanje u politici vrednuje se prema istini, dostojanstvu osobe i općem dobru, a ne samo prema uspjehu, financiranju ili koalicijskoj snazi; Crkva također ne smije biti svedena na stranački instrument. Pavlov poziv da se odbace gnjev, pogrdne riječi i zlonamjernost, te da se govori ono što drugima koristi, izravno je mjerilo za politički nastup.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage warns of the possible exploitation of national frustrations and therefore recognizes a real moral risk, but at the same time portrays rudeness and brazenness as political capital without a clear distancing from such tactics. It is especially necessary to distinguish the description of political strategy from its endorsement and to reject collective accusations against Serbs or other groups.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic participation in politics is evaluated according to truth, the dignity of the person, and the common good, not solely by success, funding, or coalition strength; neither should the Church be reduced to a partisan instrument. Paul's exhortation to put away anger, abusive language, and malice, and to speak what is beneficial to others, is a direct standard for political conduct.
concerns_en: Turning roughness, impudence, and insolence into a political advantage is in tension with Christian requirements for charity, justice, and civic speech.

Narratives about a "lost Croatia" and governance by "Yugoslavs and Serbs" can foster fear, prejudice, or hostility toward entire groups; warning against their exploitation is important, but the passage does not sufficiently elaborate on how to prevent such harm.

sections.subtitle_en: Igor Štimac: an insolent footballer as a possible unifier of the right
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić describes how Igor Štimac can translate football insolence into political capital
sections.content_en:
Marić opens the topic of **Igor Štimac**, who declared himself a future unifier of the right, and asks how his project would differ ideologically from Most and Domovinski pokret, that is, whether it would be a supra-ideological gathering.

Žižić recalls that Štimac had several appearances in influential right-wing media outlets: on a very influential podcast and on the show of an influential right-wing activist. On the podcast, he said that entering politics was not yet decided, while on the other show he said he was definitely entering. After that, he was no longer in the media, so Žižić believes that nothing is certain yet.

### Roughness as political capital

Štimac, Žižić explains, can use his recognizability, posture, roughness, and insolence. He is the epitome of an **insolent, rough footballer** who is also a tough guy on the pitch. That is what is sought after in politics today: roughness, insolence, and cheekiness, especially on social networks. That is why he can translate that into political capital.

The problem is **financial capital**. Who will finance all that and provide the infrastructure? The infrastructure on the right, apart from HDZ, according to Žižić, is held only by Most, and Most will not go with him because it stands at 10 percent and does not need Štimac. Štimac would therefore need to gather fragmented, splintered options. Regarding DP, Penava, and Dabro, he expresses himself quite favorably, and it is also evident that he is close to DOMiNO. There are also marginal rights-party options, sovereignists, and non-party individuals. There is potential, Žižić emphasizes, but the question of money and infrastructure remains open.

### Honest toward HDZ

Most promising, according to Žižić, is Štimac's clear message: **“We want to save HDZ from defeat”**, along with the open admission that HDZ is their natural coalition partner. In that, he is more honest than some other options. For now, only the outlines of his political option are visible. Štimac is dissatisfied with the direction of HDZ and Croatia, but he is there to change HDZ. Others did not succeed in that, and he, due to his attitude and habitus of a firm posture, could realistically be **equal to HDZ** in a potential government which he would enter in order, by his own logic, to save Croatia from the rule of SDSS, Možemo, and SDP.

Žižić also warns of the darker side of that potential. There is a right-wing electorate dissatisfied with HDZ that can easily be seduced by tales of a **lost Croatia** and how Yugoslavs and Serbs are in power again. In that, he says, people's national ideals, aspirations, frustrations, and traumas can be utilized, and even abused. Nevertheless, asking again who will finance it, he concludes that such a project is probably the **only option** for splintered parties standing at around 2 percent to accomplish anything.

sections.subtitle: Može li se desnica ujediniti? Izborni prag, preferencijski glasovi i stranke koje ne razmišljaju
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić objašnjava kako se stranke moraju prilagoditi izbornom sustavu i okrupniti da ne gube glasove
sections.content:
Marić se vraća ideologiji. U svakom izbornom ciklusu, primjećuje, ponavlja se priča o razjedinjenoj desnici koja se mora ujediniti. U hrvatskoj politici nije bilo rijetkost spajanje kontradiktornih opcija, poput HDZ-a i HSP-a, ili zajedničko svrstavanje protržišnih i izrazito socijalno orijentiranih. Slično se, dodaje, pod isti koš stavljaju HVO i HOS, iako je u praksi bilo vrlo različito. Pita je li ujedinjenje desnice promašena priča od samog početka.

Žižić odgovara pragmatično: **svakom izbornom sustavu korisno je prilagoditi se**. Kao primjer navodi Mađarsku, gdje su gotovo sve oporbene stranke odustale i prilagodile se sustavu, nakon čega je pobijedila Tisa. Bila je to, kaže, strateška odluka. Isto vrijedi za Hrvatsku: stranke se trebaju okrupniti kako ne bi trošile glasove i gubile ono 1 do 2 posto koji propadnu, nego okupiti se u opciju sposobnu prijeći izborni prag.

### Što ih zapravo povezuje

To je racionalno, ali Žižić upozorava da je takvo povezivanje **kratkoročno** i služi odgovoru na izazove izbornog sustava. Što takve stranke povezuje? Želja da se izbore za ulazak u Sabor, što je i samo po sebi legitimno. Pozivi na ujedinjenje desnice javljaju se osobito kad je HDZ na vlasti, jer tada ostaje dosta prostora. Žižić očekuje da će se to dogoditi na idućim izborima i smatra taj pragmatičan potez donekle razumljivim. Neki pojedinci samostalno nikad ne bi ušli u Sabor, ali na zajedničkoj listi mogu proći **preferencijskim glasovima**. Zato očekuje snažan pritisak na okrupnjavanje.

### Gospodarstvo, EU, Rusija, Izrael

Marić ostaje skeptičan. Upravo zbog ideološke nejasnoće, kad se svi deklariraju kao desničari ili konzervativci bez jasnog sadržaja, takvo okupljanje dugoročno može donijeti još veći razdor. Primjer je Domovinski pokret, koji je osvojio pristojan broj mandata pa se raspao. Nabraja teme oko kojih ne vidi zajednički nazivnik: gospodarsku politiku i ulogu države, a Žižić primjećuje da ona kod nas ionako ne utječe na izborno opredjeljenje, te vanjsku politiku, Europsku uniju, Rusiju i Izrael.

Žižić odgovara upozorenjem: **„Nemojmo precjenjivati političke stranke.“** Upitno je razmišlja li se u nekima o tim pitanjima uopće. Odmah dodaje da stranke ne treba ni podcjenjivati. One su vrlo važne za demokraciju, prema Ustavu su svojevrsno političko dobro, a dobro je što ih država javno financira. Ipak, u mnogim strankama o takvim pitanjima razmišlja se vrlo malo. Žive iz dana u dan, baveći se time kako privući pozornost, kako biti u medijima i što je medijima privlačno. Marić to sažima pojmom **influencerska politika**, koja bi, šali se, bila ideologija sama za sebe.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim shvaćanjem da je sudjelovanje u demokratskom životu legitimno i važno te da katolici mogu birati među različitim političkim opcijama koje poštuju vjeru i naravni moralni zakon. Ipak, naglasak na izbornom pragu i koristi koalicija ostaje pragmatičan: katolička procjena politike traži i jasno usmjerenje prema općem dobru, a ne samo uspjeh na izborima.
concerns: Kad se političko povezivanje prikazuje prvenstveno kao način ulaska u Sabor ili očuvanja mandata, postoji opasnost da se politika svede na taktičku korist, a da se nedovoljno razmatra služi li zajednički program ljudskom dostojanstvu i općem dobru.

Odlomak tu opasnost djelomično prepoznaje kritikom ideološke nejasnoće i influencerske politike; sama razlika u gospodarskim ili vanjskopolitičkim stajalištima, međutim, nije automatski moralni problem.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk ne propisuje jednu stranku ni jedinstveno rješenje za sva politička pitanja: različiti programi mogu biti legitimni kada su spojivi s vjerom i naravnim moralnim zakonom. Istodobno, politička sloboda nije moralna ravnodušnost; stranke i koalicije valja prosuđivati prema tome promiču li istinu, pravdu, solidarnost i opće dobro.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding that participation in democratic life is legitimate and important, and that Catholics can choose among various political options respecting faith and natural moral law. Still, the emphasis on the electoral threshold and the benefit of coalitions remains pragmatic: a Catholic evaluation of politics also requires a clear orientation toward the common good, not just electoral success.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching does not prescribe a single party or uniform solution for all political questions: diverse programs can be legitimate when compatible with faith and natural moral law. At the same time, political freedom is not moral indifference; parties and coalitions must be judged according to whether they promote truth, justice, solidarity, and the common good.
concerns_en: When political alignment is portrayed primarily as a way to enter Parliament or preserve seats, there is a risk that politics is reduced to tactical utility, without sufficient consideration of whether the joint program serves human dignity and the common good.

The passage partially recognizes this risk by criticizing ideological vagueness and influencer politics; however, mere difference in economic or foreign policy positions is not an automatic moral problem.

sections.subtitle_en: Can the right unite? Electoral threshold, preferential votes, and parties that do not think
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić explains how parties must adapt to the electoral system and consolidate so as not to lose votes
sections.content_en:
Marić returns to ideology. In every election cycle, he observes, the story repeats itself about a disunited right that must unite. In Croatian politics, the merger of contradictory options was not a rarity, such as HDZ and HSP, or the joint alignment of pro-market and strongly socially oriented forces. Similarly, he adds, HVO and HOS are thrown into the same basket, even though in practice it was very different. He asks whether the unification of the right is a failed story from the very beginning.

Žižić responds pragmatically: **it is beneficial to adapt to any electoral system**. As an example, he cites Hungary, where almost all opposition parties gave up and adapted to the system, after which Tisza won. It was, he says, a strategic decision. The same applies to Croatia: parties need to consolidate so as not to waste votes and lose that 1 to 2 percent that goes to waste, but rather gather into an option capable of crossing the electoral threshold.

### What actually connects them

That is rational, but Žižić warns that such an alliance is **short-term** and serves to answer the challenges of the electoral system. What connects such parties? The desire to fight for entry into the Sabor, which is legitimate in itself. Calls for the unification of the right appear especially when HDZ is in power, because then plenty of room remains. Žižić expects that this will happen in the next elections and considers this pragmatic move somewhat understandable. Some individuals on their own would never enter the Sabor, but on a joint list they can make it through **preferential votes**. That is why he expects strong pressure toward consolidation.

### Economy, EU, Russia, Israel

Marić remains skeptical. Precisely because of ideological vagueness, when everyone declares themselves as right-wingers or conservatives without clear substance, such a gathering in the long run can bring even greater discord. An example is Domovinski pokret, which won a decent number of mandates and then fell apart. He lists topics around which he does not see a common denominator: economic policy and the role of the state—with Žižić noting that in our country it does not influence electoral choice anyway—as well as foreign policy, the European Union, Russia, and Israel.

Žižić responds with a warning: **“Let us not overestimate political parties.”** It is questionable whether these issues are thought about in some of them at all. He immediately adds that parties should not be underestimated either. They are very important for democracy; under the Constitution, they are a kind of political public good, and it is good that the state finances them publicly. Yet, in many parties, very little thought is given to such questions. They live from day to day, concerning themselves with how to attract attention, how to be in the media, and what is appealing to the media. Marić summarizes this with the term **influencer politics**, which, he jokes, would be an ideology in its own right.

sections.subtitle: HDZ-ov utemeljiteljski resurs i paradoks državnog financiranja distribucije tiska
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić govori o Plenkovićevoj kritici pristranih medija i Vladinoj odluci o financiranju distribucije privatnog tiska
sections.content:
Marić pita kako će se HDZ ideološki pozicionirati u idućem ciklusu, s obzirom na to da je u posljednje vrijeme vrlo fleksibilan: po potrebi se pjeva Thompson, a po potrebi se nastupa liberalno.

Žižić ističe da HDZ ima postojano biračko tijelo snažno vezano uz stranku, ali i **reputacijski resurs** koji nitko drugi nema: povezanost sa stvaranjem hrvatske države. Taj **utemeljiteljski element** donosi zalihu glasova od otprilike 20 posto, možda i nešto manje, samo po toj osnovi. Usporediv je, smatra Žižić, jedino s **Afričkim nacionalnim kongresom** u Južnoj Africi: ANC je stvorio demokratsku Južnu Afriku oslobođenu apartheida, a HDZ samostalnu hrvatsku državu izvan Jugoslavije. Kad Marić spomene 300.000 članova, Žižić ga ispravlja da ih je nešto manje, oko 210.000 do 220.000, uz sve pripadajuće mreže. Ipak, upozorava, HDZ se ne smije uspavati i osloniti na to kao na nešto sigurno.

### Plenković, Klauški i pristrani mediji

Žižić zatim prepričava temu svoje nove kolumne u Glasu Koncila. Plenković je u godišnjem izvješću o radu Vlade govorio o **negativnoj percepciji** stanja u Hrvatskoj i rada Vlade te ustvrdio da dio medijske scene otvoreno i pristrano djeluje politički angažirano protiv HDZ-ove Vlade. Pritom se pozvao na doktorat novinara 24 sata **Tomislava Klauškog**, obranjen prije više od dvije godine, o kojem je Žižić tada pisao. Istraživanje je potvrdilo pristranost političkih novinara. Prema Žižićevu prepričavanju Plenkovićevih riječi, od 21 ispitanog novinara tek jedan glasuje za HDZ, dok ih velika većina, oko 70 posto, glasuje za Možemo i SDP. Premijer je to iznio kao potvrdu da kreatori javnog mnijenja stvaraju negativnu sliku.

### Država plaća distribuciju tim istim novinama

Žižić tu upozorava na paradoks. Vlada je, kako navodi, u travnju ili svibnju 2025. donijela odluku o **preuzimanju financiranja distribucije privatnog tiska**, koja se provodi od srpnja prošle godine. Klauškijevo istraživanje obuhvatilo je novinare Slobodne Dalmacije, Jutarnjeg lista, Večernjeg lista, 24 sata i Novog lista. Ti su novinari dominantno lijevo-liberalni i glasuju za SDP i Možemo, a Vlada javnim novcem financira distribuciju upravo tih novina. Žižić to naziva vrlo zanimljivim.

Istodobno podsjeća na nešto što se često zaboravlja: **lijevo-liberalni mediji nemaju željeni učinak na hrvatsko društvo**. Da ga imaju, nikad ne bi bilo Thompsonova koncerta na zagrebačkom Hipodromu. Marić dodaje da bi se moglo nabrojati i mnogo drugih primjera.

Žižić zaključuje da Vlada očito sve rješava kroz **raspodjelu sredstava**, što Marić opisuje kao hranjenje svih. Svima se daje kako bi bili zadovoljni, a opet su nezadovoljni i stvaraju probleme. Hoće li taj model biti održiv, ostaje da se vidi.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi političke i medijske procjene koje same po sebi ne proturječe katoličkom nauku, a rasprava o javnom financiranju i djelovanju stranaka legitimna je tema građanskog promišljanja. Ipak, procjena medija prema političkoj orijentaciji novinara ili popularnosti pojedinog događaja ne pokazuje sama po sebi služi li politika istini i općem dobru, pa takve tvrdnje ostaju empirijske, a ne teološke prosudbe.
concerns: Povezivanje povijesne uloge stranke s trajnom zalihom glasova opisuje politički identitet, ali ne uspostavlja moralnu opravdanost njezine sadašnje politike; katolička procjena zahtijeva razmatranje konkretnih postupaka i programa.
Tvrdnja da koncert ili drugi popularni događaj pokazuje ograničen učinak određenih medija nije dostatna moralna ili teološka argumentacija i može pojednostaviti složenu društvenu stvarnost.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko društveno naučavanje priznaje legitimnost različitih političkih opcióna i medijskih debata, ali poziva na odgovornost prema istini, ljudskom dostojanstvu i općem dobru. Javne potpore i raspodjelu sredstava stoga valja procjenjivati prema pravednosti, transparentnosti i služenju zajednici, a ne samo prema tome jesu li politički korisne ili popularne.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents political and media assessments that in themselves do not contradict Catholic teaching, and discussion of public funding and party activity is a legitimate subject of civic reflection. However, evaluating media by journalists' political orientation or the popularity of a specific event does not in itself show whether policy serves truth and the common good, so such claims remain empirical rather than theological judgments.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic social teaching recognizes the legitimacy of diverse political options and media debates, but calls for responsibility toward truth, human dignity, and the common good. Public subsidies and resource allocation should therefore be judged by justice, transparency, and service to the community, not merely by whether they are politically advantageous or popular.
concerns_en: Linking a party's historical role to a permanent reservoir of votes describes political identity, but does not establish the moral justification of its current policy; Catholic evaluation requires examining concrete actions and programs.
The claim that a concert or other popular event shows the limited impact of certain media is not sufficient moral or theological argumentation and can oversimplify a complex social reality.

sections.subtitle_en: HDZ's foundational resource and the paradox of state financing of print distribution
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić speaks about Plenković's criticism of biased media and the Government's decision to finance the distribution of private print media
sections.content_en:
Marić asks how HDZ will position itself ideologically in the next cycle, given that recently it has been very flexible: Thompson is sung as needed, and a liberal stance is taken as needed.

Žižić emphasizes that HDZ has a steady voter base strongly tied to the party, but also a **reputational resource** that no one else has: the connection with the creation of the Croatian state. That **foundational element** brings a reserve of votes of roughly 20 percent, perhaps slightly less, solely on that basis. It is comparable, Žižić believes, only to the **African National Congress** in South Africa: the ANC created a democratic South Africa freed from apartheid, and HDZ created an independent Croatian state outside Yugoslavia. When Marić mentions 300,000 members, Žižić corrects him that it is somewhat less, around 210,000 to 220,000, along with all associated networks. Still, he warns, HDZ must not become complacent and rely on this as something certain.

### Plenković, Klauški, and biased media

Žižić then recounts the topic of his new column in Glas Koncila. Plenković, in his annual report on the work of the Government, spoke about the **negative perception** of the situation in Croatia and the work of the Government, asserting that a portion of the media scene openly and biasedly acts politically engaged against the HDZ Government. In doing so, he referred to the doctoral dissertation of 24 sata journalist **Tomislav Klauški**, defended more than two years ago, about which Žižić wrote at the time. The research confirmed the bias of political journalists. According to Žižić's retelling of Plenković's words, out of 21 surveyed journalists, only one votes for HDZ, while the vast majority, around 70 percent, vote for Možemo and SDP. The Prime Minister presented this as confirmation that public opinion creators are producing a negative image.

### The state pays for the distribution of those same newspapers

Here Žižić points out a paradox. The Government, as he states, made a decision in April or May 2025 on **taking over the financing of the distribution of private print media**, which has been implemented since July of last year. Klauški's research covered journalists from Slobodna Dalmacija, Jutarnji list, Večernji list, 24 sata, and Novi list. Those journalists are predominantly left-liberal and vote for SDP and Možemo, while the Government finances the distribution of those very newspapers with public money. Žižić calls this very interesting.

At the same time, he recalls something that is often forgotten: **left-liberal media do not have the desired effect on Croatian society**. If they did, there would never have been Thompson's concert at the Zagreb Hippodrome. Marić adds that many other examples could also be listed.

Žižić concludes that the Government obviously resolves everything through the **allocation of funds**, which Marić describes as feeding everyone. Everyone is given something so that they would be satisfied, yet they are dissatisfied again and create problems. Whether that model will be sustainable remains to be seen.

sections.subtitle: Dvije političke apoteoze i tema koju nitko ne otvara: uloga države i uvoz opasnog otpada
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić pripovijeda kako mu u reciklažnom dvorištu važu auto, dok stotine tisuća tona opasnog otpada ulaze bez kontrole
sections.content:
Na pitanje o realnim koalicijskim raspletima Žižić je oprezan. Do redovitih izbora ima još godinu i pol, a mnogo toga se može dogoditi što se sada ne da predvidjeti. Ipak, izdvaja ono što je opisao u svojoj kolumni kao **dvije političke apoteoze**, uzdizanje dvojice političara:

- **Tomislava Tomaševića**, kao najizglednijeg kandidata SDP-a i Možemo za predsjednika Vlade;
- **Igora Štimca**, koji se uzdiže kao vođa desnice.

To su procesi koje namjerava pratiti u skorije vrijeme. Sve ostalo smatra teškim i nezahvalnim za predviđanje.

### Što je ostalo od države?

Kad Marić pita koje bi teme mogle obilježiti kampanju, Žižić izražava želju da se više razgovara o **ulozi države**: što je danas od nje preostalo. Kao primjer navodi suočavanje s **masovnim ilegalnim odlaganjem opasnog otpada**. Tada se pokazalo da je to područje potpuno deregulirano i liberalizirano. Država više nema kontrolu, digla je ruke od kontroliranja i reguliranja, a Hrvatska uvozi stotine tisuća tona otpada za koji se ne zna gdje završi.

Žižić to ilustrira osobnom anegdotom. Kad nosi madrac u reciklažno dvorište, auto mu se važe na ulazu i na izlazu, što smatra sasvim u redu: kontrola tako i treba izgledati. Istodobno, kaže, stotine tisuća tona opasnog otpada ulaze u zemlju bez ikakve kontrole. Marić se našali da madrac nije opasan, pa bi s opasnim otpadom bilo drugačije. Žižić inzistira da kontrolni mehanizmi moraju postojati, a ovdje ih je država napustila. Razlog vidi u **vladajućoj paradigmi otvaranja i dereguliranja**, u kojoj je ideja što manja uloga države i prepuštanje svega deregulaciji.

### Rat o prošlosti umjesto rasprave o budućnosti

Žižić se ipak boji da će kampanju ponovno obilježiti **rat o prošlosti**. Kao suprotan primjer navodi AfD u Njemačkoj, koji napreduje i zato što je u jednom trenutku shvatio da gubi kad govori o prošlosti. U Hrvatskoj je, naprotiv, dominantna ideja upravo razgovora o prošlosti. Postojat će suprotstavljene interpretacije povijesnih zbivanja, ali prošlost se ne može ni promijeniti ni popraviti, a nitko neće prihvatiti tuđu interpretaciju.

Zato bi Žižić radije da se raspravlja o pitanjima budućnosti:

- što će ostati od države;
- hoće li se Hrvatska potpuno ekonomski otvoriti;
- kako se postaviti prema **masovnom priljevu strane radne snage**;
- gledaju li građani na probleme kao članovi političke zajednice i solidarni kršćani ili samo kao **potrošači**.

Ako pobijedi potrošačka logika, zaključuje Žižić, to će koristiti jedino Možemo.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na država treba štititi zajedničko dobro, nadzirati štetne djelatnosti i poticati solidarnost uglavnom je sukladan katoličkom socijalnom nauku. Ipak, konkretne tvrdnje o uvozu otpada i ocjena da bi potrošačka logika koristila jedino određenoj stranci ostaju političke procjene, a ne zaključci koje sam po sebi potvrđuje katolički nauk.
concerns: Ne treba poistovjetiti katolički socijalni nauk s jednim određenim modelom regulacije: tekst ne razrađuje kako uskladiti odgovornost države, gospodarsku slobodu i načelo supsidijarnosti.
Tvrdnja da bi pobjeda potrošačke logike koristila jedino Možemo stranačka je procjena, a ne teološki utemeljena tvrdnja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko promišljanje politike polazi od služenja zajedničkom dobru, uz kompetentno i odgovorno obnašanje javne vlasti; konkretne političke prosudbe pritom mogu legitimno varirati. magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that the state should protect the common good, regulate harmful activities, and foster solidarity is largely consistent with Catholic social teaching. Still, concrete claims about waste importation and the assessment that consumer logic would benefit only a specific party remain political assessments, not conclusions confirmed in themselves by Catholic teaching.

Regarding migration, teaching speaks both of the duty to welcome, as far as possible, the foreigner in search of safety and means of livelihood, and of the right of political authorities to regulate immigration for the sake of the common good.
concerns_en: One should not equate Catholic social teaching with a single specific regulatory model: the text does not elaborate on how to balance state responsibility, economic freedom, and the principle of subsidiarity.

sections.subtitle_en: Two political apotheoses and a topic that no one brings up: the role of the state and the import of hazardous waste
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić narrates how his car is weighed at the recycling yard, while hundreds of thousands of tons of hazardous waste enter without control
sections.content_en:
When asked about realistic coalition outcomes, Žižić is cautious. There is still a year and a half until the regular elections, and many things can happen that cannot be predicted now. Still, he singles out what he described in his column as **two political apotheoses**, the rise of two politicians:

- **Tomislav Tomašević**, as the most likely candidate of SDP and Možemo for Prime Minister;
- **Igor Štimac**, who is rising as the leader of the right.

These are processes that he intends to follow in the near future. Everything else he considers difficult and ungrateful to predict.

### What is left of the state?

When Marić asks what topics could mark the campaign, Žižić expresses a wish that more discussion take place about the **role of the state**: what remains of it today. As an example, he cites the confrontation with the **massive illegal disposal of hazardous waste**. At that time, it became apparent that this area was completely deregulated and liberalized. The state no longer has control, it washed its hands of controlling and regulating, and Croatia imports hundreds of thousands of tons of waste for which it is unknown where it ends up.

Žižić illustrates this with a personal anecdote. When he takes a mattress to the recycling yard, his car is weighed at the entrance and at the exit, which he considers completely fine: that is how control should look. At the same time, he says, hundreds of thousands of tons of hazardous waste enter the country without any control. Marić jokes that a mattress is not hazardous, so with hazardous waste it would be different. Žižić insists that control mechanisms must exist, and here the state has abandoned them. He sees the reason in the **ruling paradigm of opening and deregulating**, in which the idea is as minimal a role of the state as possible and leaving everything to deregulation.

### A war over the past instead of a debate about the future

Žižić nevertheless fears that the campaign will again be marked by a **war over the past**. As a contrasting example, he cites the AfD in Germany, which is progressing also because at one point it realized that it loses when speaking about the past. In Croatia, on the contrary, the dominant idea is precisely discussing the past. There will be conflicting interpretations of historical events, but the past can neither be changed nor repaired, and no one will accept someone else's interpretation.

That is why Žižić would rather see debates about questions of the future:

- what will remain of the state;
- whether Croatia will completely open up economically;
- how to approach the **massive influx of foreign labor**;
- whether citizens view problems as members of a political community and solidary Christians, or merely as **consumers**.

If consumer logic wins, Žižić concludes, that will benefit only Možemo.

sections.subtitle: Pristojni političari skriveni iza verbalne pirotehnike
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić govori o pristojnim i kompetentnim ljudima u hrvatskoj politici koje zasjenjuje verbalna pirotehnika
sections.content:
Pri kraju razgovora Marić primjećuje da su bili kritični prema većini političkih opcija i pojava. Izražava nadu da ih nitko neće krivo shvatiti jer politiku promatraju iz šire, objektivne perspektive. Zato pita postoji li nešto pozitivno u hrvatskoj političkoj kulturi što Žižića veseli.

Žižić odmah naglašava da **nije negativan prema hrvatskoj politici**, dapače. Smatra da u njoj ima jako mnogo **pristojnih, marljivih, kompetentnih i odgovornih ljudi**. To se, nažalost, ne vidi jer je medijska slika politike negativna i usmjerena samo na ono što je grubo, drsko, bezobrazno i uvredljivo.

Odgovornost pritom ne svaljuje samo na medije. Mediji, kaže, vide da publika takve sadržaje klika, pa ih i nude. Volio bi da se više prati i vrednuje **ozbiljan rad u politici**, a ne ono što naziva **verbalnom pirotehnikom** u Saboru ili drugdje: napadanje, provociranje i grubost kojima se dobiva pažnja. Upravo bi to, zaključuje, trebalo promijeniti.

magisterium.assessment: Isticanje poštenih, marljivih i odgovornih političara te kritika vrijeđanja i verbalne agresije dobro se slažu s kršćanskim zahtjevom za poštovanjem političkih protivnika i razumijevanjem politike kao služenja. Odlomak je više opći etički komentar nego izričito izlaganje katoličkog nauka, ali ne sadržava očito naukovno odstupanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan Pavao II. naglašava da kršćansko političko djelovanje treba obilježavati poštovanje prema onima koji misle drukčije, kao i istinoljubivost u javnom životu. Katolička tradicija politiku opisuje kao mogući oblik služenja drugima i zajedničkom dobru, koji zahtijeva moralnu dosljednost i odgovornost, a ne puku borbu za pozornost ili glasove.

sections.subtitle_en: Decent politicians hidden behind verbal pyrotechnics
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić speaks about decent and competent people in Croatian politics who are overshadowed by verbal pyrotechnics
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the conversation, Marić notes that they were critical of most political options and phenomena. He expresses hope that no one will misunderstand them because they observe politics from a broader, objective perspective. Therefore, he asks whether there is anything positive in Croatian political culture that pleases Žižić.

Žižić immediately emphasizes that he is **not negative toward Croatian politics**, on the contrary. He believes that there are very many **decent, hardworking, competent, and responsible people** in it. That, unfortunately, is not seen because the media portrayal of politics is negative and directed only at what is rough, insolent, cheeky, and offensive.

In doing so, he does not place the responsibility solely on the media. The media, he says, see that the audience clicks on such content, so they offer it. He would like to see **serious work in politics** monitored and valued more, rather than what he calls **verbal pyrotechnics** in the Sabor or elsewhere: attacking, provoking, and roughness through which attention is gained. Precisely that, he concludes, should be changed.

sections.subtitle: Poruka biračima: Hrvatska je zrela nacionalna država, ali gdje su poluge državne vlasti?
sections.screenshot_description: Jakov Žižić poručuje biračima da je Hrvatska zrela nacionalna država te postavlja pitanje poluga državne vlasti
sections.content:
Na kraju Marić traži poruku biračima: na što obraćati pažnju i na čemu inzistirati. Žižić polazi od postignutog. Hrvati su stvorili svoju državu, nacionalno im nitko ne može uzeti i Hrvatska je **zrela nacionalna država**. Opisuje je kao stabilnu i održivu zajednicu koja je socijalno uključiva i ekonomski prosperitetna te jasno orijentirana prema Zapadu, kao članica Europske unije i NATO-a.

Poziva da se Hrvatska prestane uspoređivati s Jugoslavijom, koju naziva vrlo neuspješnom državom. Komunistička Jugoslavija trajala je 45 godina, a Hrvatska je već prošla 35. Marić se nadovezuje pitanjem tko bi 1980. rekao da je Jugoslavija mlada država, a Žižić potvrđuje: Hrvatska je prešla velik put i **ozbiljna je nacionalna država**. Nitko je, ističe, neće staviti u nikakve nove balkanske tvorevine.

### Država kao jamstvo opstanka nacije

Otvoreno pitanje, naglašava Žižić, nije opstanak države nego način na koji se koriste **poluge državne vlasti**. Hoće li Hrvatska biti država koja vodi aktivnu politiku, nešto regulira i uređuje ono što se događa unutar njezinih granica? To ovisi o građanima: gledaju li na stvari kao **članovi političke zajednice ili kao potrošači**.

Naglašava da svaki čovjek ima jednako dostojanstvo i jednaku vrijednost. Ipak, ne može biti svejedno ako će se svi problemi rješavati stranom radnom snagom, dodatnim dereguliranjem i ekonomskim otvaranjem. Tada se, pita Žižić, gubi trag polugama državne vlasti. Država je, zaključuje, **jamstvo opstanka nacije**.

### Odjava

Marić zahvaljuje Jakovu Žižiću na trećem gostovanju i izražava nadu da će se vidjeti i četvrti put. Gost uzvraća zahvalom na pozivu. Voditelj zatim poziva gledatelje da podrže kanal lajkom, dijeljenjem i pretplatom. Ističe da je jedini i glavni cilj takvog sadržaja **oplemenjivanje hrvatskog političkog diskursa i političke kulture** te poziva sve koji su spremni ući u tu bitku da ih nastave pratiti. Razgovor završava pozdravom „Živjeli!“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim društvenim naukom jer naglašava dostojanstvo svake osobe, političku odgovornost građana i legitimnu ulogu države u uređivanju zajedničkog života. Ipak, formulaciju da je država „jamstvo opstanka nacije” treba tumačiti ograničeno: država služi osobi i općem dobru, a nacionalno dobro ne smije se postaviti iznad dostojanstva stranaca ni međunarodne solidarnosti.
concerns: Izraz „država je jamstvo opstanka nacije” može zvučati kao da je država apsolutna ili jedini čuvar nacionalnog identiteta. Katolički nauk priznaje vrijednost nacije, ali državu podređuje služenju osobama, prirodnim zajednicama, općem dobru i miru.

Kritika rješavanja problema stranom radnom snagom i deregulacijom legitimna je kao rasprava o politici i zajedničkom dobru, ali ne smije prijeći u sumnjičenje ili isključivanje stranih radnika kao skupine. Crkveni nauk istodobno priznaje pravo vlasti da razborito uređuje migracije i obvezu da se prema migrantima postupa ljudski, uz poštovanje njihove jednake dostojanstvenosti.

Tvrdnje o tome da je Hrvatska „zrela” i „ozbiljna” država te da je neće uključiti u nove političke tvorevine jesu političke procjene i predviđanja, a ne tvrdnje koje se mogu vrednovati kao katolički nauk ili biblijsko učenje.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijska i crkvena perspektiva priznaje vrijednost građanske vlasti: Rim 13, kako ga tumači Papinska biblijska komisija, potiče poštovanje vlasti i javnih dužnosti, ali pod uvjetom da vlast djeluje pravedno i ostane unutar svojih legitimnih granica. Katolički nauk također dopušta vlastima da migracije uređuju radi općega dobra, ma non nega l’obbligo di accogliere con umanità chi cerca sicurezza e mezzi di sussistenza; la Scrittura richiama l’amore per lo straniero e per il prossimo. Pertanto, la nazione può essere amata e la comunità politica attivamente governata, ma il patriottismo cristiano non deve diventare nazionalismo esclusivo: deve restare aperto alla dignità di ogni persona e alla solidarietà fra popoli.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic social teaching because it emphasizes the dignity of each person, the political responsibility of citizens, and the legitimate role of the state in ordering collective life. However, the formulation that the state is the "guarantee of the nation's survival" must be interpreted restrictively: the state serves the person and the common good, and national good must not be placed above the dignity of foreigners or international solidarity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical and Church perspectives recognize the value of civil authority: Romans 13, as interpreted by the Pontifical Biblical Commission, encourages respect for authority and public duties, but on condition that authority acts justly and remains within its legitimate boundaries. Catholic teaching also allows authorities to regulate migration for the common good, but does not deny the obligation to welcome with humanity those seeking safety and means of livelihood; Scripture recalls love for the stranger and neighbor. Therefore, the nation can be loved and the political community actively governed, but Christian patriotism must not become exclusive nationalism: it must remain open to the dignity of every person and solidarity among peoples.
concerns_en: The expression "the state is the guarantee of the nation's survival" can sound as though the state is absolute or the sole guardian of national identity. Catholic teaching recognizes the value of the nation, but subordinates the state to serving persons, natural communities, the common good, and peace.

Criticizing the resolution of problems through foreign labor and deregulation is legitimate as a debate on policy and the common good, but must not cross into suspicion or exclusion of foreign workers as a group. Church teaching simultaneously recognizes the right of authorities to prudently regulate migration and the obligation to treat migrants humanely, with respect for their equal dignity.

Claims that Croatia is a "mature" and "serious" state and that it will not be included in new political entities are political assessments and predictions, not assertions that can be evaluated as Catholic teaching or biblical instruction.

sections.subtitle_en: A message to voters: Croatia is a mature nation-state, but where are the levers of state power?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Jakov Žižić sends a message to voters that Croatia is a mature nation-state and raises the question of the levers of state power
sections.content_en:
In the end, Marić asks for a message to the voters: what to pay attention to and what to insist upon. Žižić starts from what has been achieved. Croats created their state, no one can take the national away from them, and Croatia is a **mature nation-state**. He describes it as a stable and sustainable community that is socially inclusive and economically prosperous, and clearly oriented toward the West, as a member of the European Union and NATO.

He calls for Croatia to stop comparing itself to Yugoslavia, which he calls a very unsuccessful state. Communist Yugoslavia lasted 45 years, and Croatia has already passed 35. Marić follows up with the question of who in 1980 would have said that Yugoslavia was a young state, and Žižić confirms: Croatia has traveled a long road and is a **serious nation-state**. No one, he emphasizes, will place it into any new Balkan constructs.

### The state as a guarantee of the survival of the nation

The open question, Žižić emphasizes, is not the survival of the state, but the manner in which the **levers of state power** are used. Will Croatia be a state that pursues an active policy, regulates something, and orders what happens within its borders? That depends on the citizens: whether they look at things as **members of a political community or as consumers**.

He emphasizes that every human being has equal dignity and equal worth. Nevertheless, it cannot be a matter of indifference if all problems are going to be solved through foreign labor, additional deregulation, and economic opening. Then, Žižić asks, the trace of the levers of state power is lost. The state is, he concludes, **a guarantee of the survival of the nation**.

### Sign-off

Marić thanks Jakov Žižić for his third guest appearance and expresses hope that they will see each other a fourth time. The guest returns thanks for the invitation. The host then invites viewers to support the channel with a like, share, and subscription. He points out that the sole and primary goal of such content is the **enrichment of Croatian political discourse and political culture**, and invites all who are ready to enter that battle to continue following them. The conversation ends with the greeting “Živjeli!”.
